# Zenvi tools

<!-- Generated by packages/engine/scripts/gen-tools-doc.ts from @zenvi/engine/tools. Do not edit by hand. -->

One tool catalog for every Zenvi surface: the Zenvi Assistant in the web editor, the local MCP server (`zenvi mcp`), the Zenvi Cloud remote MCP server, and the CLI. 252 tools: 164 of the 169 tools Zenvi desktop lists (zenvi-core develop `1f80cb3d061b`; same names, arguments and receipts) and 88 direct tools for coding agents. The other desktop tools are not ported yet (see [Not ported yet](#not-ported-yet)).

Every call returns a contract-3 receipt (`{contract: 3, status, tool, summary, clips, …, undoSteps}`); a failure's summary starts with `Error:`, and a surface limitation says `Error: <tool> is not available in this Zenvi surface: …` (do not retry). One call is at most one undo step.

## Where tools work

| Surface | Host | Works | Partial | Not available |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Web editor (Zenvi Assistant, command palette) | `apps/editor/src/features/editor/assistant/host.ts` | 161 | 50 | 41 |
| CLI and local MCP server (zenvi, zenvi mcp) | `packages/render-node/src/host/node-host.ts` | 194 | 29 | 29 |
| Zenvi Cloud remote MCP server (ChatGPT, Claude.ai) | `packages/cloud/src/mcp/engine.ts` | 158 | 43 | 51 |
| Zenvi desktop | zenvi-core | 164 | 0 | 88 (direct tools are web-only) |

Availability follows each tool's required host capabilities and the host methods it calls at run time; the hosts are described in `SURFACE_PROFILES` (packages/engine/src/tools/availability.ts). Capabilities a session may lack (signed out of Zenvi, no WebCodecs export) are noted per tool.

- **Web editor (Zenvi Assistant, command palette)**: media, player, ui, exporter, frames, backend, stock, storage, assets, audio, library; methods media.importUrl, media.pickFiles, media.writeGenerated, media.missing, storage.readText, storage.writeText, storage.writeBytes, storage.exportMedia, storage.currentPath, storage.recentProjects, ui.openExportDialog, audio.decodePcm, audio.mixPcm, audio.transcribe, ui.selection, ui.setSelection, ui.timelineView, ui.showTimelineRange, ui.setTimelineMode, ui.layout, ui.preferences, ui.clearPlaybackCache, exporter.supports; only sometimes: exporter (browsers with WebCodecs export), backend (signed in to Zenvi), stock (signed in to Zenvi).
- **CLI and local MCP server (zenvi, zenvi mcp)**: media, exporter, frames, audio, storage, backend, stock, assets, mattes, motion, scenes3d, fx, library, watch; methods media.importPath, media.listPaths, media.importUrl, media.writeGenerated, media.missing, media.fetchWebVideo, media.kitSample, media.inspectRender, media.decodeLuma, storage.open, storage.readText, storage.writeText, storage.writeBytes, storage.saveCopy, storage.readCopy, storage.exportMedia, storage.currentPath, storage.recentProjects, storage.recoveryCopies, storage.customProfiles, media.collect, audio.decodePcm, audio.mixPcm, audio.transcribe, audio.generateSfx, exporter.supports, frames.fontFamilies, frames.renderSheet, frames.sampleFrames, audio.measureMix; only sometimes: backend (signed in with zenvi login), stock (signed in with zenvi login), media.fetchWebVideo (yt-dlp is installed; zenvi doctor checks), audio.generateSfx (ELEVENLABS_API_KEY is set to a key on a paid ElevenLabs plan), mattes (onnxruntime-node is installed; the matting model downloads on first use), audio.transcribe (zenvi speech setup ran (on device, free), else signed in with zenvi login), motion (headless Chrome is installed: zenvi motion setup), scenes3d (Blender 4.2+ is installed (or ZENVI_BLENDER points to it)), fx (ffmpeg is installed (ZENVI_FX=0 turns it off)), watch (signed in with zenvi login (or ZENVI_GEMINI_API_KEY is set, for development)).
- **Zenvi Cloud remote MCP server (ChatGPT, Claude.ai)**: media, frames, storage, assets, audio, backend, stock, exporter, mattes, motion, watch; methods media.importUrl, media.writeGenerated, media.missing, storage.readText, storage.writeText, storage.writeBytes, storage.exportMedia, storage.currentPath, storage.recentProjects, audio.decodePcm, audio.mixPcm, audio.transcribe, frames.fontFamilies, exporter.supports; only sometimes: frames (the render worker is configured), exporter (the render worker is configured), media (ffprobe is available), assets (the engine's assets (title templates, emoji) are bundled), audio (ffmpeg is available), audio.mixPcm (ffprobe is available), backend (the server is set up to call the Zenvi backend), stock (the server calls the Zenvi backend, or has its own PEXELS_API_KEY / FREESOUND_API_KEY), mattes (onnxruntime-node is in the image (the matting model downloads on first use; up to 10 s of video per call)), motion (the image has chrome-headless-shell (one block renders at a time)), watch (the server calls the Zenvi backend and has ffmpeg; the render must be media in the project's bin); hides 17 local-app tools.

## Tools

### get_project_info_tool

**Read project info**. Return project profile, fps, duration, and scale.

Surfaces: assistant, mcp, cli, editor. read-only.

Availability: editor yes; cli yes; cloud yes; desktop yes.

No arguments.

### list_files_tool

**List project media**. List media-bin files (paths, ids) — not timeline positions.

Surfaces: assistant, mcp, cli, editor. read-only.

Availability: editor yes; cli yes; cloud yes; desktop yes.

No arguments.

### list_clips_tool

**List clips**. List timeline clips with source_start/end, summary_preview, and occurrence_hint when duplicates exist.

Surfaces: assistant, mcp, cli, editor. read-only.

Availability: editor yes; cli yes; cloud yes; desktop yes.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `layer` | string |  | Optional layer_number or UI track filter. |
| `detail_level` | string |  | summary (default) or full — accepted for Assistant/LLM compat; listing is always complete. |

### list_layers_tool

**List tracks**. List tracks/layers (ui_track and layer_number).

Surfaces: assistant, mcp, cli, editor. read-only.

Availability: editor yes; cli yes; cloud yes; desktop yes.

No arguments.

### list_markers_tool

**List markers**. List every marker in the project.

Surfaces: assistant, mcp, cli, editor. read-only.

Availability: editor yes; cli yes; cloud yes; desktop yes.

No arguments.

### new_project_tool

**New project**. Create a new empty project.

Surfaces: assistant, mcp, cli, editor. edits, destructive.

Availability: editor yes; cli yes; cloud — (hidden: belongs to a local app); desktop yes.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `discard_unsaved` | boolean |  | Throw away unsaved changes in the current project. Only after the user agreed. (default false) |
| `profile` | string |  | Optional video profile or social preset for the new project, e.g. 'instagram_reel', 'youtube_4k', 'FHD 1080p 30 fps' (see list_project_profiles_tool). Empty = default profile. (default "") |
| `save_first` | boolean |  | Save the current project to its existing file first (it must have been saved before). (default false) |

### save_project_tool

**Save project**. Save the project to file_path (e.g.

Surfaces: assistant, mcp, cli, editor. edits, destructive. Needs: storage.

Availability: editor yes; cli yes; cloud — (hidden: belongs to a local app); desktop yes.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `file_path` | string |  | Where to save. Empty = the project's current file (Save). A new path = Save As (.zvn is added when there is no project extension; missing folders are created). (default "") |
| `overwrite` | boolean |  | Allow replacing an existing file that is not this project's current file. (default false) |
| `path` | string |  | Where to save the project (.zvn is appended when missing). Omit to save to the current location. |

### open_project_tool

**Open project**. Open a project from file_path.

Surfaces: assistant, mcp, cli, editor. edits, destructive. Needs: storage.

Availability: editor — (needs opening project files); cli yes; cloud — (hidden: belongs to a local app); desktop yes.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `discard_unsaved` | boolean |  | Throw away unsaved changes in the current project. Only after the user agreed. (default false) |
| `file_path` | string |  | Path of a .zvn project (legacy .osp/.flow also open). Leave empty when using recent_index. (default "") |
| `recent_index` | integer |  | Open a recent project instead: 1 = most recent (see list_recent_projects_tool). 0 = use file_path. (default 0, min 0, max 10) |
| `save_first` | boolean |  | Save the current project to its existing file before opening the other one. (default false) |

### watch_clip_tool

**Load and play clip**. Play a clip in the editor preview: seek to a timeline clip (timeline_clip_id or query) and start playback.

Surfaces: assistant, mcp, cli, editor. edits. Needs: player.

Availability: editor partial (file_path needs local file access); cli — (needs playback); cloud — (hidden: belongs to a local app); desktop yes.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `file_path` | string |  | Media path to import, place and play. |
| `query` | string |  | Describe the timeline clip to play. |
| `file_id` | string |  | Media-bin file to play (added to the timeline when it is not there yet). |
| `timeline_clip_id` | string |  | Timeline clip to play. |

### watch_clip_window_tool

**Watch clip window**. Vision-check whether a query is actually visible in a window of a placed clip.

Surfaces: assistant, mcp, cli, editor. read-only, open world. Needs: frames, backend.

Availability: editor yes (only when signed in to Zenvi); cli yes (only when signed in with zenvi login); cloud yes (only when the render worker is configured and the server is set up to call the Zenvi backend); desktop yes.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `query` | string |  | What should be on screen in the window. |
| `start` | string \| number |  | Window start, source seconds (12, 12.5 or 0:12). Give start and end together, or neither to watch the best search match. |
| `end` | string \| number |  | Window end, source seconds. |
| `timeline_clip_id` | string |  | Timeline clip id (from list_clips_tool, get_timeline_state_tool or an earlier receipt). |
| `clip_query` | string |  | Describe the clip instead of passing an id: file name, subject, or words from its summary. Narrow it with track, occurrence or position_near. |
| `track` | string |  | Track: layer_number (preferred), track_id, the exact label, or ui_track counted from the bottom (1 = bottom). |
| `occurrence` | string \| number |  | 1-based pick when the query matches the same source several times (0 = best match). |
| `position_near` | string \| number \| null |  | Timeline seconds; only clips that span this time match. |

### play_tool

**Play / pause**. Control preview playback: action play, pause, toggle (default, like the Space bar), stop (pause and return to the start), or step_forward / step_back by frames.

Surfaces: assistant, mcp, cli, editor. read-only. Needs: player.

Availability: editor yes; cli — (needs playback); cloud — (hidden: belongs to a local app); desktop yes.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `action` | "toggle" \| "play" \| "pause" \| "stop" \| "fast_forward" \| "rewind" \| "step_forward" \| "step_back" |  | What to do. play / pause (always pass one of these for a plain 'play' or 'pause'); toggle = the Space bar; stop = pause and return to the start; fast_forward / rewind = the L / J keys (one speed step faster forward / backward); step_forward / step_back = pause and move by `frames`. (default "toggle") |
| `frames` | integer |  | For step_forward / step_back: how many frames to move. (default 1, min 1, max 10000) |
| `speed` | integer \| null |  | For action='play': playback speed, 1 = normal, 2 or 4 = fast, -1 = backwards. Omit for normal speed. (min -16, max 16) |

### add_track_tool

**Add track**. Add empty tracks: on top (default, like the Add Track button), at the bottom, or above / below the track in relative_to.

Surfaces: assistant, mcp, cli, editor. edits.

Availability: editor yes; cli yes; cloud yes; desktop yes.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `count` | integer |  | How many tracks to add in this one step. With a name they are called '<name> 1' .. '<name> N' from bottom to top. (default 1, min 1, max 10) |
| `name` | string |  | Name shown in the new track's header, e.g. 'Music'. Empty = the default 'Track N'. (default "") |
| `position` | "top" \| "bottom" \| "above" \| "below" |  | Where the new track goes: 'top' (above every track, like the Add Track button), 'bottom' (below every track), or 'above' / 'below' the track in relative_to (Track menu > Add Track Above / Below). (default "top") |
| `relative_to` | string |  | For position 'above' / 'below': the existing track, as a UI track number (1 = bottom), track name, track id (L3) or layer number. (default "") |
| `label` | string |  | Alias for name. |

### add_marker_tool

**Add marker**. Add a timeline marker at position_seconds (default: the playhead), with a name and a colour tag.

Surfaces: assistant, mcp, cli, editor. edits.

Availability: editor yes; cli yes; cloud yes; desktop yes.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `color` | "blue" \| "red" \| "green" \| "yellow" \| "orange" \| "purple" \| "pink" \| "white" |  | Marker color tag; the timeline tints the marker's icon with it (blue = the default icon) and shows the marker's name next to it. (default "blue") |
| `name` | string |  | Marker name, e.g. 'Drop', 'Chorus', 'Cut here'. Used to find it again. (default "") |
| `position_seconds` | number \| null |  | Timeline seconds for the marker (0:32 = 32, 1:05 = 65). Omit to mark the playhead position. (min 0) |
| `label` | string |  | Alias for name. |
| `text` | string |  | Alias for name. |

### delete_from_timeline_tool

**Delete from timeline**. Delete from the timeline: one clip placement, or an entire track.

Surfaces: assistant, mcp, cli, editor. edits, destructive.

Availability: editor yes; cli yes; cloud yes; desktop yes.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `timeline_clip_id` | string |  | Timeline clip id (from list_clips_tool, get_timeline_state_tool or an earlier receipt). |
| `clip_query` | string |  | Describe the clip instead of passing an id: file name, subject, or words from its summary. Narrow it with track, occurrence or position_near. |
| `track` | string |  | Track: layer_number (preferred), track_id, the exact label, or ui_track counted from the bottom (1 = bottom). |
| `scope` | "auto" \| "clip" \| "track" |  | auto (default): a clip id/query deletes one placement, a bare track clears the track. clip / track force the branch. (default "auto") |
| `occurrence` | string |  | 1-based pick when the query matches the same source several times (0 = best match). (default "0") |
| `position_near` | string \| number \| null |  | Timeline seconds; only clips that span this time match. |
| `include_transitions` | boolean |  | Track scope only: also delete transitions on the track (default true). (default true) |
| `ripple` | string \| boolean |  | One clip only: true closes the gap it leaves (later items on that track move left); default false leaves the gap. (default false) |

| `style` | "boxed" \| "classic" \| "minimal" \| "reels" \| "yellow" |  | Look preset: classic = white text on a dark box at the bottom (subtitles); reels = big bold white text with a black outline (Instagram/TikTok/Shorts); minimal = small white text with a thin outline; yellow = yellow text with a black outline (TV subtitles); boxed = white on a solid black box. The arguments below override parts of it. (default "classic") |

| `transition` | string |  | Transition between consecutive clips: '' = hard cuts, 'fade' = crossfade, 'random', or a transition name such as 'wipe_left_to_right' or 'circle_in_to_out' (list_transitions_tool). (default "") |

### analyze_frame_colors_tool

**Analyze colors**. Measure a frame the way the scopes do, as numbers, to grade objectively and to check that an effect or grade did what was asked: luma percentiles p1-p99 and mean (0 = black, 1 = white), clipped shadows/highlights %, mean RGB, warmth (R-B), green/magenta balance, the white-balance cast of near-neutral pixels (neutral_tint_uv, cast label), saturation_mean (HSV 0-1: <0.12 muted, 0.2-0.4 natural, >0.55 very saturated), chroma (UV), gray_pct (100 = black and white), transparent_pct (share keyed out / transparent), a plain-words verdict and suggested_grade values for color_grade_clip_tool.

Surfaces: mcp, cli, editor. read-only. Needs: frames.

Availability: editor partial (save_frame_path attaches the frame to the result instead of writing a file; frames are measured at most 960 px wide); cli partial (save_frame_path attaches the frame to the result instead of writing a file; frames are measured at most 960 px wide); cloud partial (save_frame_path attaches the frame to the result instead of writing a file; frames are measured at most 960 px wide; only when the render worker is configured); desktop yes.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clip_query` | string |  | Describe the clip instead of an id: its file name or what it shows (e.g. 'beach sunset'). Add track when several clips match. Prefer timeline_clip_id. (default "") |
| `compare_without_effects` | boolean |  | Also analyze the same frame with the effects removed (before/after). (default false) |
| `region` | object |  | Only this part of the frame: {"x", "y", "width", "height"} as fractions 0-1 (e.g. a face or the sky). |
| `save_frame_path` | string |  | Also save the analyzed frame as a PNG at this absolute path (to look at it). (default "") |
| `time` | number \| null |  | Timeline seconds to analyze (default: the clip's middle, or the playhead for the whole timeline). |
| `timeline_clip_id` | string |  | Timeline clip id from list_clips_tool / get_timeline_state_tool. Preferred. (default "") |
| `track` | string |  | Narrow clip_query to a track: UI track number (1 = bottom), track name, or layer number. (default "") |
| `whole_timeline` | boolean |  | Analyze the composite of every track at `time` instead of one clip alone. (default false) |

### color_grade_clip_tool

**Color grade**. Color grade clips with the Color Grade effect: a named look ("make it cinematic", "teal and orange", "warm it up", "cooler", "vintage", "black and white", "film noir", "moody", "vibrant", "bright and airy"), a LUT, and/or exact controls (exposure, contrast, highlights, shadows, saturation, vibrance, temperature, tint, wheels, curves).

Surfaces: mcp, cli, editor. edits.

Availability: editor partial (a .cube file outside the built-in LUTs needs local file access); cli yes; cloud partial (a .cube file outside the built-in LUTs needs local file access); desktop yes.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clip_query` | string |  | Describe the clip instead of an id: its file name or what it shows (e.g. 'beach sunset'). Add track when several clips match. Prefer timeline_clip_id. (default "") |
| `contrast` | number \| null |  | Contrast. Range -1..1; leave out to keep the current/look value. (min -1, max 1) |
| `curves` | object |  | Tone curves {"all"\|"red"\|"green"\|"blue": [[x, y], ...]} with input->output points in 0-1, e.g. an S-curve {"all": [[0,0],[0.25,0.2],[0.75,0.82],[1,1]]}; 'reset' flattens. |
| `exposure` | number \| null |  | Brightness in stops (+0.3 = brighter). Range -2..2; leave out to keep the current/look value. (min -2, max 2) |
| `highlights` | number \| null |  | Bright areas (negative recovers blown skies). Range -1..1; leave out to keep the current/look value. (min -1, max 1) |
| `look` | "" \| "auto_contrast" \| "black_and_white" \| "boost_color" \| "bright_airy" \| "cinematic" \| "cool" \| "film_noir" \| "golden_hour" \| "lift_shadows" \| "moody" \| "natural" \| "neutral" \| "teal_orange" \| "vibrant" \| "vintage" \| "warm" \| "warm_up" |  | Named grade: neutral = every control neutral, no LUT (undo a grade); natural = gentle contrast S-curve, a little vibrance; auto_contrast = Look > Color > Auto Contrast; lift_shadows = Look > Color > Lift Shadows (open up dark footage); warm_up = Look > Color > Warm Up; boost_color = Look > Color > Boost Color; cinematic = blockbuster teal/orange LUT at 50%, contrast curve, slightly muted; teal_orange = strong teal shadows / orange skin tones; warm = warmer white balance; golden_hour = sunset orange glow; cool = cooler, bluer; vintage = faded film, lifted blacks; black_and_white = monochrome with a little contrast; film_noir = hard-contrast black and white; moody = darker, desaturated, cold shadows; vibrant = punchy saturated color; bright_airy = light, soft, lifted. Starts from neutral; the other arguments then adjust it. (default "") |
| `lut` | string |  | LUT to apply: a name from list_luts_tool ('teal & orange cinema', 'film_stock_&_vintage/classic_film'), a .cube path, or 'none' to remove it. (default "") |
| `lut_intensity` | number \| null |  | How strongly the LUT applies. Range 0..1; leave out to keep the current/look value. (min 0, max 1) |
| `mix` | number \| null |  | Grade strength: 1 = full, 0.5 = half-way to the original. Range 0..1; leave out to keep the current/look value. (min 0, max 1) |
| `reset` | boolean |  | Start from a neutral grade instead of the clip's current one. (default false) |
| `saturation` | number \| null |  | Color intensity: 1 = unchanged, 0 = black and white. Range 0..4; leave out to keep the current/look value. (min 0, max 4) |
| `scope` | "" \| "selected" \| "track" \| "all" |  | Instead of ids/query: 'selected' = timeline selection, 'track' = every clip on `track`, 'all' = every clip. Clips that cannot take the effect (locked track, no picture/sound) are skipped and listed. (default "") |
| `shadows` | number \| null |  | Dark areas (positive lifts them). Range -1..1; leave out to keep the current/look value. (min -1, max 1) |
| `temperature` | number \| null |  | White balance: + warmer (orange), - cooler (blue). Range -1..1; leave out to keep the current/look value. (min -1, max 1) |
| `timeline_clip_id` | string |  | Timeline clip id from list_clips_tool / get_timeline_state_tool. Preferred. (default "") |
| `timeline_clip_ids` | string[] |  | Several timeline clip ids to change in one step. |
| `tint` | number \| null |  | White balance: + magenta, - green. Range -1..1; leave out to keep the current/look value. (min -1, max 1) |
| `track` | string |  | Narrow clip_query to a track: UI track number (1 = bottom), track name, or layer number. (default "") |
| `vibrance` | number \| null |  | Boosts muted colors more than saturated ones. Range -1..1; leave out to keep the current/look value. (min -1, max 1) |
| `wheels` | object |  | Color wheels, e.g. {"shadows": {"color": "#2a6cff", "amount": 0.15}, "highlights": {"color": "#ffb36b", "amount": 0.12, "luma": 0.02}}: tint color, amount 0-1, luma -1..1 per wheel (global, shadows, midtones, highlights). |

### process_clip_effect_tool

**Stabilize / track / detect**. Run an analysis effect on a video clip, off the GUI thread, and add the result as an effect: "stabilize the shaky shot" (Stabilizer), "track the ball / the car" (Tracker with a region box), "detect people" (ObjectDetection, YOLO), "cut out the person / mask the dog" (ObjectMask with points or a box).

Surfaces: mcp, cli, editor. edits.

Availability: editor — (needs OpenCV clip analysis (Stabilizer, Tracker, Object Detector, Object Mask) (Zenvi desktop)); cli — (needs OpenCV clip analysis (Stabilizer, Tracker, Object Detector, Object Mask) (Zenvi desktop)); cloud — (needs OpenCV clip analysis (Stabilizer, Tracker, Object Detector, Object Mask) (Zenvi desktop)); desktop yes.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `boxes` | object[] |  | ObjectMask: box(es) around the object, [{"x", "y", "width", "height"}] (fractions). |
| `class_filter` | string |  | ObjectDetection: only show these labels, comma separated ('person,car'). (default "") |
| `clip_query` | string |  | Describe the clip instead of an id: its file name or what it shows (e.g. 'beach sunset'). Add track when several clips match. Prefer timeline_clip_id. (default "") |
| `confidence` | number \| null |  | ObjectDetection: minimum confidence 0-1 (default 0.25). (min 0, max 1) |
| `device` | "CPU" \| "GPU_AUTO" \| "GPU_CUDA" \| "GPU_OPENCL" |  | ObjectDetection/ObjectMask processing device. (default "CPU") |
| `download_model` | boolean |  | Download the model files if missing (Object Detector ~10-90 MB, Object Mask ~175 MB, from the OpenShot model releases, sha256-verified). (default false) |
| `effect` | "Stabilizer" \| "Tracker" \| "ObjectDetection" \| "ObjectMask" | yes | Stabilizer = remove camera shake; Tracker = follow a boxed object; ObjectDetection = find people/cars/animals... (YOLO); ObjectMask = cut out an object you point at. |
| `if_exists` | "auto" \| "update" \| "add" |  | If the clip already has this effect: auto = replace a Stabilizer/Object Detector, add another Tracker/Object Mask; update = replace; add = keep both. (default "auto") |
| `interpolation` | "bezier" \| "linear" \| "constant" |  | Default interpolation for keyframes that do not name one. (default "bezier") |
| `mask_quality` | "" \| "cutie-low" \| "cutie-medium" \| "cutie-high" |  | ObjectMask Cutie tracking quality ('' = recommended medium). (default "") |
| `model` | "" \| "yolo26n-seg" \| "yolo26s-seg" \| "yolo26m-seg" \| "yoloe-26n-seg" \| "yoloe-26s-seg" \| "yoloe-26m-seg" \| "yolo11n-seg" \| "yolo11s-seg" \| "yolo11m-seg" |  | ObjectDetection model ('' = recommended YOLO26 Nano; yoloe-* know more labels). (default "") |
| `negative_points` | object[] |  | ObjectMask: points NOT on the object (background). |
| `points` | object[] |  | ObjectMask: points ON the object, [{"x": 0.5, "y": 0.4}] (fractions). |
| `properties` | object |  | Effect properties to set, as {name: value}. A value is a number, true/false, a choice name ("HSV/HSL hue"), a color ("#00ff00") or text; or keyframes [{"time": 2.0, "value": 10, "interpolation": "linear"}] in timeline seconds to animate it. list_effects_tool(effect=...) lists every property with its range, default and choices. |
| `region` | object |  | Tracker: box around the object at region_time, {"x", "y", "width", "height"} as fractions of the frame (0,0 = top-left). |
| `region_time` | number \| null |  | Tracker/ObjectMask: timeline seconds of the frame the region/points refer to (default: the clip's first frame). |
| `smoothing` | integer |  | Stabilizer: frames averaged, 1-100 (30 default; higher = steadier, more crop). (default 30, min 1, max 100) |
| `timeline_clip_id` | string |  | Timeline clip id from list_clips_tool / get_timeline_state_tool. Preferred. (default "") |
| `timeout_seconds` | number |  | Give up (changing nothing) after this long. (default 900, min 5, max 3600) |
| `track` | string |  | Narrow clip_query to a track: UI track number (1 = bottom), track name, or layer number. (default "") |
| `tracker_type` | "KCF" \| "CSRT" \| "MIL" \| "BOOSTING" \| "TLD" \| "MEDIANFLOW" \| "MOSSE" |  | Tracker algorithm: KCF fast (default), CSRT most accurate, MOSSE fastest. (default "KCF") |

### update_transition_tool

**Change transition**. Change a transition on the timeline: length, position, wipe shape, softness, curves, audio crossfade.

Surfaces: mcp, cli, editor. edits.

Availability: editor yes; cli yes; cloud yes; desktop yes.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `at_seconds` | number \| null |  | Instead of ids: the transition under this timeline time (on `track` when given). (min 0) |
| `audio_crossfade` | boolean \| null |  | Also crossfade the two clips' audio under the transition (equal-power). |
| `between_clip_ids` | string[] |  | Instead of ids: the two timeline clip ids the transition joins, e.g. [clip_a, clip_b]. |
| `brightness_keyframes` | object[] |  | Replace the progress curve (brightness): 1 = not started, -1 = finished; times from the transition start. |
| `contrast` | number \| null |  | Edge hardness of the wipe: 0 = very soft/blurry edge, 3 = the default soft edge, 20 = a hard line. (min 0, max 20) |
| `contrast_keyframes` | object[] |  | Replace the edge-hardness curve over time. |
| `duration_seconds` | number |  | New length in seconds (0 = keep). On a crossfade between two clips the later clip moves so the clips overlap by exactly this much (see keep_overlap). (default 0, min 0) |
| `flip_wipe_side` | boolean |  | Wipe from the other side (left-to-right becomes right-to-left, circle-out becomes circle-in) and still go from the earlier clip to the later one. Works for any mask (inverts it and reverses its curve). (default false) |
| `interpolation` | "" \| "bezier" \| "linear" \| "constant" |  | Easing of the progress curve: bezier = ease in/out (default), linear = constant speed, constant = jump. '' = keep. (default "") |
| `invert_mask` | boolean \| null |  | Raw 'mask invert' property. Alone it makes the later clip show first (it flashes back before the cut); use flip_wipe_side instead. |
| `keep_overlap` | boolean |  | With duration_seconds on a crossfade: do not move any clip (the transition may then run past the overlap and dip to the track below). (default false) |
| `mask` | string |  | Change the wipe shape: a transition name ('fade', 'wipe_left_to_right', 'circle_in_to_out', any list_transitions_tool name) or an image file path. '' = keep. (default "") |
| `mask_file_id` | string |  | Use this project image file (e.g. a gradient or logo) as the wipe shape. '' = keep. (default "") |
| `position_seconds` | number \| null |  | Move the transition to start at this timeline time (clips stay). (min 0) |
| `replace_image` | boolean \| null |  | Show the mask image itself instead of transitioning (a preview aid). |
| `ripple` | boolean |  | With duration_seconds on a crossfade: move everything after the later clip on that track too, so no gap or overlap opens further down. false = move only the later clip. (default true) |
| `scope` | "" \| "selected" \| "track" \| "all" |  | 'selected' = selected transitions, 'track' = every transition on `track`, 'all' = every transition on the timeline. (default "") |
| `track` | string |  | Track to look on (UI track number, 1 = bottom; name; or layer number). With scope='track' every transition on it. (default "") |
| `transition_ids` | string[] |  | Transition ids (list_timeline_transitions_tool or get_timeline_state_tool 'Effects/Transitions'). Preferred. |

### master_audio_tool

**Master audio** (direct tool). Measure the timeline's mix (integrated loudness LUFS, true peak, per-role levels) and gain-stage it to a delivery target so it is loud, clean and balanced: dialogue anchors the mix, music sits under it and ducks while someone talks, SFX stay over the bed.

Surfaces: mcp, cli, editor. edits, destructive. Needs: audio.

Availability: editor yes; cli yes; cloud yes (only when ffmpeg is available and ffprobe is available); desktop — (web-only direct tool).

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `preset` | "social" \| "broadcast" \| "podcast" |  | Delivery target: social = -14 LUFS / -1 dBTP (Reels, TikTok, Shorts), broadcast = -23 LUFS (EBU R128), podcast = -16 LUFS. (default "social") |
| `target_lufs` | number |  | Integrated loudness to reach, LUFS. Overrides the preset's. (min -40, max -6) |
| `true_peak_dbtp` | number |  | True-peak ceiling, dBTP. Overrides the preset's. (min -9, max 0) |
| `balance` | "auto" \| "keep" |  | auto: dialogue anchors the mix, music sits under it (ducked while someone talks), SFX accents over the bed. keep: keep the current balance and only scale the mix. (default "auto") |
| `duck` | boolean |  | Duck music/ambience under speech where it is not already ducked (the same envelope as duck_under_speech_tool). (default true) |
| `speech_clip_ids` | string \| string[] |  | Clips that carry dialogue, when they are not indexed (otherwise unclassified clips count as music). |
| `music_clip_ids` | string \| string[] |  | Clips to treat as music. |
| `sfx_clip_ids` | string \| string[] |  | Clips to treat as sound effects. |
| `dry_run` | boolean |  | Measure and plan only: report the loudness before and after, change nothing. (default false) |
| `genre` | "hype" \| "flash_montage" \| "saas_ui" \| "talking_head" \| "match_cut" \| "product_3d" \| "video_essay" \| "editorial" \| "multiplicity" \| "general" |  | The Sound Score's target bands (analyze_mix_tool genre) for score and iterate. (default "general") |
| `score` | boolean |  | Score the mastered mix with analyze_mix_tool's Sound Score (in data.score). (default true) |
| `limit` | boolean |  | When the true-peak ceiling stops the mix short of the target, ride the frames that peak down (volume keyframes: the music and ambience under a hit up to 10 dB, else every clip playing there up to 4 dB; a look-ahead limiter the desktop plays too), so the mix gets there. (default true) |
| `iterate` | boolean |  | Before mastering, run analyze_mix_tool's loop: apply its top fixes and re-score, up to 3 rounds, until 85+ with no gate failed; a round that lowers the score is dropped. The whole run is one undo step. (default false) |

### analyze_mix_tool

Score the timeline's sound (the Zenvi Sound Score, 0-100): renders the mix and each stem (voice, music, sfx, ambience) and measures loudness LUFS / true peak / LRA / crest, voice over the bed while speaking, SFX and music masking the voice, spectral balance, phone and mono translation, hit-point coverage and cue timing, cue prominence by role, repetition and density, each against the genre's target band, with the exact fix as tool calls (set_audio_gain_tool, duck_tool, automate_volume_tool, eq_tool, compress_tool, move_clip_tool, add_sfx_tool, master_audio_tool).

Surfaces: mcp, cli, editor. read-only. Needs: audio.

Availability: editor yes; cli yes; cloud yes (only when ffmpeg is available and ffprobe is available); desktop — (web-only direct tool).

(default "general") |

| `shape` | "points" \| "dip" \| "ramp" \| "swell" \| "suck_out" \| "pre_hit_duck" \| "swell_between_lines" \| "fade_in" \| "fade_out" | yes | points: your (t, db) keyframes. dip: db (default -6) from start to end with fade_ms ramps. ramp: 0 dB at start to db at end, held to the clip's end. swell: up db (default +2) and back over start-end. suck_out: the bed drops db (default -18) for length_ms (200) before the at_seconds / hit_times hit(s), 20 ms fall, 10 ms return. pre_hit_duck: db (-10) for length_ms (120) before each hit (default: every hero cue). swell_between_lines: +db (default +2) on the bed between voice lines at least 600 ms apart. fade_in / fade_out: from / to silence over length_ms at the clip's start / end. |
| `points` | object[] |  | shape=points: the keyframes, timeline seconds. |

| `db` | number |  | The shape's depth or height, dB. (min -60, max 12) |

| `fade_ms` | number |  | dip / swell_between_lines: ramp time at each edge, ms (default 50 / 150). (min 0, max 5000) |
| `curve` | "linear" \| "bezier" \| "constant" |  | Segment shape for the generated points (default linear; swell defaults to bezier). |
| `mode` | "relative" \| "absolute" |  | relative (default): dB over the current curve, keeping ducks and fades; absolute: dB re unity replace the curve inside the span. (default "relative") |

| `release_ms` | number |  | Ramp back up, ms (default voice 400, heroes 250). (min 0, max 4000) |
| `lookahead_ms` | number |  | Start the duck this early, ms (default voice 50, heroes 10). (min 0, max 1000) |
| `dry_run` | boolean |  | Measure and plan only. (default false) |

### eq_tool

**EQ** (direct tool). Equalise clips, a track or a stem by number with libopenshot's Parametric EQ (one effect per band): high-pass rumble off, carve a 3 kHz pocket in the music for the voice, add air to the SFX, muffle a bed.

Surfaces: mcp, cli, editor. edits, destructive.

Availability: editor partial (Zenvi desktop's libopenshot Parametric EQ computes its filters from the samples per frame instead of the sample rate, so the desktop hears these bands at other frequencies until that is fixed); cli partial (Zenvi desktop's libopenshot Parametric EQ computes its filters from the samples per frame instead of the sample rate, so the desktop hears these bands at other frequencies until that is fixed); cloud partial (Zenvi desktop's libopenshot Parametric EQ computes its filters from the samples per frame instead of the sample rate, so the desktop hears these bands at other frequencies until that is fixed); desktop — (web-only direct tool).

| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `track` | string \| number |  | Every clip with sound on this track: layer_number, track id, exact label (e.g. 'SFX'), or ui_track. |
| `role` | "voice" \| "music" \| "sfx" \| "ambience" |  | Every clip of this stem: voice, music, sfx, ambience (analyze_mix_tool lists each clip's; set_track_role_tool sets a track's). |
| `bands` | object[] |  | Up to 4 bands. |
| `preset` | "clean_low" \| "voice_clarity" \| "voice_pocket" \| "presence" \| "air" \| "muffle" \| "phone" \| "none" |  | clean_low: high-pass by stem (voice 90, ambience 150, micro SFX 300, music / other SFX 40 Hz). voice_clarity: HPF 90 + 3.5 kHz +2 dB. voice_pocket: 3 kHz -3 dB, Q 1 (music under VO). presence: 4 kHz +3 dB. air: high shelf +2.5 dB at 8 kHz. muffle: low-pass 800 Hz (through-the-wall). phone: 300 Hz-3.4 kHz. none: remove this tool's EQ. |

### build_reel_tool

**Build a reel** (direct tool). Cut a finished short-form video (Reels, TikTok, Shorts, ads) in one step from media already in the project: shots cut on the music's beats, camera moves, flashes, a look, an opening hook title, shot labels, an end card and the music faded out.

Surfaces: mcp, cli, editor. edits, destructive. Needs: media.

Availability: editor yes; cli yes; cloud yes (only when ffprobe is available); desktop — (web-only direct tool).

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `style` | "hype" \| "cinematic" \| "highlight" \| "match_cut" \| "minimal" \| "editorial" \| "retro" \| "ui_promo" \| "editorial_motion" \| "product_callout" \| "tutorial" |  | How the reel is cut and looks (default hype). hype: Energetic montage for launches, sports, events and travel: fast cuts on the beat, flashes on the downbeats, punchy colour. cinematic: Moody, filmic montage for stories, brands and places: steady 2-beat shots, slow push-ins, grain, fades. highlight: The best moments of the person's own clips (games, trips, events): cut on the beat, building to the big moment. match_cut: Shots that share a shape or pose cut on every beat (circles, hands, horizons): the frame stays still so the shapes line up. minimal: Slow, airy edit for wellness, food, interiors and products: long holds, gentle moves, soft fades. editorial: Graphic, magazine-like cut for fashion, design and tech: crisp cuts on 1/2 beats, labels on the shots, clean contrast. retro: Nostalgic camcorder feel for vlogs, throwbacks and music: tape artefacts, warm colour, super 8 grain. ui_promo: Motion-designed product promo for apps and tools: a search bar types the hook, footage rises in rounded UI cards and a pointer clicks, a word list scrolls in a selection box, a logo end card. Give `words` for the word list. editorial_motion: Graphic specimen-sheet motion for fashion, design, food and objects: the hook as big kinetic type on a gridded sheet (a letter swapped for an image tile), labelled crop boxes over a shot that lift into a row, kinetic words, a closing card. Red, black and paper with one blue. product_callout: Technical product reveal: each product shot on a dark field with a soft glow, an 'ANATOMY: NAME' heading, leader lines drawing out to feature labels, one per beat, then a closing card. Give `words` as features ('Foam core: 212 g'). tutorial: A how-to in steps: the hook on grid paper, then each step's footage in a bordered card with a numbered caption and a label box with an arrow, ending on 'Save this'. 9:16 first. One step per label: the caption from `labels` (clips that share a label are one step), the arrow's box from `words`, one word per step. |
| `file_ids` | string[] |  | Media-bin videos and images to use, in story order; the last one closes the reel. Bin order is not a story order: get one from sequence_shots_tool (dry_run: true, its data.file_ids). Default: every video and image in the bin (not SVG titles), in bin order. |
| `music_file_id` | string |  | Music in the media bin to cut to. Default: the longest audio file in the bin. Without music the cuts follow the style's own tempo. |
| `duration_seconds` | number |  | Target length, seconds (default per style, 12-20). The reel ends on a bar line: the first at or after it (at most a bar longer), else the nearest; the summary says the final length and why. (min 4, max 120) |
| `hook` | string |  | Opening title over the first shots: 2-6 punchy words. |
| `end_card` | string |  | Closing title over the last shot (a call to action, a name, a date). |
| `end_card_subtitle` | string |  | A smaller line under the end card. |
| `labels` | string[] |  | Small labels shown on each file's shots, in file_ids order ("" for none). Motion styles: the card captions (ui_promo), crop labels (editorial_motion), step captions (tutorial). |
| `words` | string[] |  | Motion styles only: the scrolling word list (ui_promo), kinetic words (editorial_motion), the features as 'Name: value' (product_callout), each step's label box (tutorial). |
| `beats` | number[] |  | Beat times of the music in seconds (e.g. from detect_beats_tool), used as they are instead of detecting the beat. |
| `bpm` | number |  | Tempo to use instead of the detected one. Alone: the music is tracked at this tempo (detect_beats_tool's alternatives lists the half/double readings). With offset_seconds: no detection, the grid is exact. (min 40, max 400) |
| `offset_seconds` | number |  | With bpm: where the first beat falls in the music, seconds. The grid runs from there at that tempo. (min 0, max 3600) |
| `replace` | boolean |  | Clear the timeline first when it already has clips (they are removed in the same undo step). |
| `keep_order` | boolean |  | Cut styles without file_ids: keep the bin's own order (by default the bin is ordered by continuity first, like sequence_shots_tool). |
| `strict_variety` | boolean |  | Refuse (nothing changes) when the files are too few for the pace and a file comes back within 3 s; the error says how many more to import. Default false: a warning. |
| `grade` | string |  | One look over every shot: 'auto' (default for hype and highlight) measures each clip, corrects it toward one target and lays one shared LUT (a cool night look when the titles say night or the footage is dark, else teal and orange); a LUT id from list_looks_tool uses that LUT; 'none' (default for the other styles) skips it. Needs a surface that renders frames. |

### align_match_cut_tool

**Align match cuts** (direct tool). Line up the shared subject of consecutive clips (an iris, the moon, a cup rim, a pose) so it sits at the same place and size on every cut: writes scale/location (and rotation) keyframes from each clip's subject box, keeps the frame covered (zooming when needed, reported) and is one undo step.

Surfaces: mcp, cli, editor. edits.

Availability: editor yes; cli yes; cloud yes; desktop — (web-only direct tool).

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clips` | object[] | yes | Timeline clips in cut order, each with its subject's box. |
| `target` | object |  | Where every subject lands. Default: where the first clip shows its subject now, on its first frame. |
| `fit` | "position" \| "position_scale" \| "position_scale_rotation" |  | position: move only; position_scale (default): move and resize so sizes match; position_scale_rotation: also turn each subject to the target angle (boxes need angle). |
| `cover` | "zoom" \| "zoom_all" \| "none" |  | Keeping the frame covered: zoom scales a clip up just enough when moving or shrinking it would show black edges (its subject ends up larger); zoom_all raises the target size for every clip so all still match; none allows black edges. |
| `zoom_drift` | number |  | Zoom each clip in by this fraction over its length, about the subject (0.04 = 4 %). Default 0. (min 0, max 0.5) |

### match_cut_montage_tool

**Match-cut montage** (direct tool). Cut a full-circle match-cut montage in one step from media-bin files that share a shape or pose (eye, moon, cup, vinyl, lens): shots of 3-8 frames on the music's hits and beats with a held first and last shot, every shot aligned so the subject sits at the same place and size, white flashes on downbeats, a motion transition once a bar between them (transitions: punch by default, flash for a flash montage, whip, none), a small zoom per shot and the music bed.

Surfaces: mcp, cli, editor. edits, destructive. Needs: media.

| `file_ids` | string[] | yes | Media-bin videos and images in chain order: the first opens (held), the last closes (held), the others cycle in between. Bin order is not a chain: get one from sequence_shots_tool (dry_run: true, continuity: 2, its data.file_ids). |
| `subjects` | object[] |  | Subject boxes per file. Files without one are searched for a circle at each shot's first frame (detect_subject_tool), or kept centred when this surface cannot read frames. |
| `music_file_id` | string |  | Music in the media bin to cut to. Default: the longest audio file in the bin. |
| `beats` | number[] |  | Beat times of the music in seconds (e.g. from detect_beats_tool), used as they are instead of detecting the beat. |
| `bpm` | number |  | Tempo to use instead of the detected one. Alone: the music is tracked at this tempo (detect_beats_tool's alternatives lists the half/double readings). With offset_seconds: no detection, the grid is exact. (min 40, max 400) |
| `offset_seconds` | number |  | With bpm: where the first beat falls in the music, seconds. The grid runs from there at that tempo. (min 0, max 3600) |
| `duration_seconds` | number |  | Target length, seconds (default: one pass through the files, at least 8 s). Ends on a downbeat. (min 2, max 60) |
| `target` | object |  | Where every subject lands. Default: the frame's centre, at the size the first file shows its subject. |
| `fit` | "position" \| "position_scale" \| "position_scale_rotation" |  | position: move only; position_scale (default): move and resize so sizes match; position_scale_rotation: also turn each subject to the target angle (boxes need angle). |
| `cover` | "zoom" \| "zoom_all" \| "none" |  | Default zoom_all: every subject the same size and no black edges. |
| `min_frames` | integer |  | Shortest body shot, frames (default 3). (min 2, max 12) |
| `max_frames` | integer |  | Longest body shot, frames (default 8). (min 2, max 24) |
| `flash` | boolean |  | A white flash frame on cuts that land on a downbeat (default true). |
| `zoom_drift` | number |  | Each shot zooms in by this fraction about its subject (default 0.04). (min 0, max 0.3) |
| `transitions` | "auto" \| "none" \| "punch" \| "flash" \| "whip" |  | Motion transitions on the cuts, once a bar between the flashed downbeats, in the same undo step: auto (default) = punch: crash zoom about the subject and glitch, the last cut flying into the subject; flash (a flash montage): inverted frames, glitches and punches; whip: whips in one direction, landing on a pull-back; none: hard cuts and flashes only. |
| `strict_variety` | boolean |  | Refuse (nothing changes) when the files are too few for the pace and a file comes back within 3 s; the error says how many more to import. Default false: a warning. |
| `replace` | boolean |  | Clear the timeline first when it already has clips (in the same undo step). |
| `keep_order` | boolean |  | Keep file_ids as given when they are the bin's own order (by default such a list is first chained by shape continuity, like sequence_shots_tool). |

### sequence_shots_tool

**Sequence shots** (direct tool). Order (and trim to slots) candidate shots the way an editor cuts them, instead of bin order: each cut carries something across (the action continues, the same shape and position, the subject where the eye already is, the colour, the motion's direction), an energy arc (peak: build, peak, release), no near-duplicate back to back, the strongest shot held for the payoff, and speaker shots on their own words in the voice-over (speech_at, or says + a transcribed voice_file_id).

Surfaces: mcp, cli, editor. edits, destructive. Needs: frames.

Availability: editor partial (without frame sampling each shot is compared on a few rendered frames (its ends and five through it), so its energy is coarser); cli yes; cloud partial (without frame sampling each shot is compared on a few rendered frames (its ends and five through it), so its energy is coarser; only when the render worker is configured); desktop — (web-only direct tool).

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `shots` | object[] |  | The candidate shots: all timeline clips, or all bin files / windows of them. |
| `file_ids` | string[] |  | Shorthand for shots: whole bin files. |
| `track` | string \| number |  | Without shots or file_ids: reorder every clip on this track (UI track number, 1 = bottom; name; or layer number). With file shots: the track to place them on (default an empty track). |
| `arc` | "build" \| "peak" \| "release" \| "flat" |  | Energy curve over the sequence: peak (default: build to a peak three quarters in, then release), build, release, flat (order by continuity alone). |
| `open` | string |  | clip_id or file_id of the shot that must open. |
| `close` | string |  | clip_id or file_id of the payoff shot that closes, or "none". Default: the strongest shot (interest and length) closes. |
| `slots` | number[] |  | Slot lengths in seconds, in timeline order (the beats of a brief, shot lengths of a plan). Shots are trimmed to them; with fewer slots than shots the weakest and duplicate shots are left out (clips removed). |
| `continuity` | number |  | Weight of cut continuity against the arc (default 1; 2 = match cuts first). (min 0, max 2) |
| `voice_file_id` | string |  | The voice-over / dialogue in the media bin that speaker shots sync to (speech_at, says; a clip of this same file syncs by itself). |
| `voice_at` | number |  | Timeline seconds where voice_file_id's audio starts (default: where a clip of it plays it, else the sequence start). (min 0) |
| `position` | number |  | File shots: timeline seconds the sequence starts at (default 0). (min 0) |
| `dry_run` | boolean |  | Only plan: return the order (data.file_ids feeds match_cut_montage_tool or build_reel_tool) without changing the timeline. |

| `color` | string |  | Stroke colour, #RRGGBB (default #FFFFFF). |

| `padding` | number |  | The graphic's box is the subject's box times this (default 1.25; 1 hugs it). (min 0.5, max 4) |
| `flip_x` | boolean |  | golden_spiral: mirror left-right (where the spiral sweeps from). |
| `flip_y` | boolean |  | golden_spiral: mirror top-bottom. |
| `spiral_height` | number |  | golden_spiral: height of its golden rectangle, fraction of the canvas height (default 1). (max 3) |
| `start` | number |  | Timeline seconds it appears (default the clip's start). (min 0) |
| `duration` | number |  | Seconds it stays (default to the clip's end). |

Reframe a clip so a tracked point (a face, a pivot foot, a product) stays at one place on the canvas while the subject moves or the shot punches in: writes scale/location keyframes from the clip's own track, zooming just enough to keep the frame covered.

Surfaces: mcp, cli, editor. edits. Needs: frames.

| `point` | object |  | A point to follow on the source frame (a face, a fingertip, a product part). Read it off a frame's 0-1 grid (inspect_media_tool, preview_frame). |
| `box` | object |  | A box to follow on the source frame (a head, a product, a UI card). |

| `zoom` | number |  | Scale relative to the clip's current scale on its first frame (default 1; 1.3 = a 130 % punch-in). (min 0.2, max 6) |
| `zoom_end` | number |  | Scale at the clip's end, ramped from zoom (a slow push about the point). Default: zoom. (min 0.2, max 6) |
| `keep_size` | boolean |  | Scale against the subject's own size so it stays the same size on screen (it walks towards camera: the frame widens). |
| `allow_edges` | boolean |  | Allow the canvas to show around the clip instead of zooming in to cover it. Default false. |

### unify_grade_tool

**Unify grade** (direct tool). Grade continuity for a whole cut: measures every footage clip's exposure, white balance and contrast on frames across it, corrects each clip's ColorGrade toward one target (a reference clip/file, or the clips' median look in a neutral band) until it sits within tolerance (saturation is reported, not matched), then optionally lays one LUT look over all of them.

Surfaces: mcp, cli, editor. edits. Needs: frames.

| `reference_clip_id` | string |  | Timeline clip whose look the others match (it is not corrected). Default: the clips' median look, pulled into a neutral band. |
| `reference_file_id` | string |  | Media-bin video or image whose look the clips match, instead of a timeline clip. |
| `strength` | number |  | Share of each correction applied, 0.1-1 (default 1). Lower keeps more of each shot's own character. (min 0.1, max 1) |
| `look` | string |  | A LUT look laid over every unified clip after the correction (list_looks_tool ids, e.g. 'teal_cinema', 'warm_cinema'), so the look lands on matched plates. |
| `look_intensity` | number |  | Strength of the look, 0-1 (default the LUT's own, 1). (min 0, max 1) |
| `samples` | integer |  | Frames measured per clip (default 5). (min 1, max 16) |
| `max_iterations` | integer |  | Measure-and-correct passes per clip (default 4; a pass that clips the picture is dropped and retried gentler). (min 1, max 6) |
| `dry_run` | boolean |  | Measure and report the corrections without changing anything. |

### add_motion_template_tool

**Add a motion template** (direct tool). Place one motion-design template on the timeline, timed to the beat: UI cards that slide in with depth, a search field that types, a scrolling word list with a selection box, labelled crop boxes over a shot, a product callout with leader lines, kinetic type with image tiles, a tutorial step card, a grid background, an end card, a cascade of video cards dropping in, a frame-locked A/B compare (split, diagonal or offset boxes), skewed parallelogram windows snapping to full bleed, a layer-pass breakdown wiped on with a travelling hairline, or footage cells reflowing between grid layouts.

Surfaces: mcp, cli, editor. edits. Needs: media.

Availability: editor yes; cli yes; cloud yes (only when ffprobe is available); desktop — (web-only direct tool).

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `template` | "ui_cards" \| "type_search" \| "word_scroll" \| "crop_labels" \| "callout" \| "kinetic_type" \| "step_card" \| "grid_background" \| "end_card" \| "grid" \| "card_cascade" \| "compare" \| "window_cascade" \| "pass_wipe" \| "reflow" | yes | Which template. ui_cards: Up to three rounded UI cards (footage or photos inside, or text cards) rise into a fan (landscape) or slide into a cascade (portrait), one per beat, with depth; with a button, a pointer glides to the front card and clicks it (press, ripple, check), then the camera pushes in. Reads file_ids (card media, in order), labels (a caption per card; a card without a file is a text card titled by its label), subtitle (text cards' second line), button (what the pointer clicks). type_search: A search field rises in, the phrase types letter by letter with a blinking caret and lands on a beat; suggestions drop open under it a row per half beat while the field glides up to make room; then the button presses (or the first suggestion is selected) and a focus ring lights up. Reads text (the phrase, one line), button (the button label), subtitle (a prompt above the field), tag (a brand row on top: its mark and name), labels (up to 4 suggestions that drop open under the field; the press selects the first), backdrop. word_scroll: A column of big words scrolls up one word per beat; each scroll lands on the beat with the word held in a selection box (handles and a size readout), the other words dimmed; an optional lead line reads into the word. Reads words (2-10, in order), text (a lead line: beside the word in landscape, above it in portrait), backdrop. crop_labels: A shot fills the frame and pushes in; labelled crop boxes snap onto it one per beat; then a paper scrim covers it and the crops lift out of the shot into labelled tiles: a row, or a column of big tiles on vertical video. Reads file_ids (the shot: the first file), boxes (frame boxes, 0-1; default a spread), labels (one per box; default DETAIL 01…), tag (the default labels' prefix), variant (boxes: no row). callout: A product shot on a dark field with a soft halo and a glowing 'ANATOMY: NAME' heading over a rule that draws on; then one callout per beat: a dot pops on the product, a leader line draws out and a label (index, name, value) slides in. On vertical video the heading stacks over a tall product frame and the labels sit above and below it. Reads file_ids (the product: the first file), text (the product name), tag (the heading's prefix, default ANATOMY), labels (callout names, 1-4), values (their second lines), points (anchors on the product picture, 0-1; its crop keeps them in view). kinetic_type: A big grotesk headline lands one word per beat, each word popping in; * in the text becomes an image tile (a word or a letter replaced by footage or a photo); optional highlighter swipe behind a word and a small tag after the last word. Reads text (the headline; * = image tile), file_ids (tile media, used in turn), highlight (word index), tag, align (left \| center), position (top \| center \| bottom). step_card: A tutorial step: the footage rises into a rounded card with an ink border and a hard shadow, a numbered caption pops in under it, then a small label box appears and an arrow draws from it to a point in the footage. Reads file_ids (the step's footage: the first file), text (the caption), step (its number, default 1), tag (the label box's text), points (where the arrow points in the footage, 0-1; the card's crop keeps it in view; default the card's upper right), subtitle (a still header at the top, e.g. the video's hook). grid_background: A still, full-frame field: grid paper (paper), an editorial sheet with column grid, ruler ticks, registration marks and corner labels (editorial), a dark dot grid (dots) or a flat colour (plain). Reads variant (paper \| editorial \| dots \| plain, default from the palette), labels (editorial: up to 4 corner labels). end_card: The closing card. logo: a brand mark pops in, the name slides out beside it, the subtitle rises; save: a bookmark drops in and 'Save this' lands with a highlighter swipe; plain: a tag, the title and the subtitle rise in turn. Draws its own backdrop. Reads text (title or brand name; save defaults to 'Save this'), subtitle, tag (plain), variant (logo \| save \| plain), align (plain), backdrop. grid: A montage of your clips in tiles that fill one per beat: a grid of 2 to 9 tiles, vertical or horizontal strips, a film strip with the big frame last, or an irregular mosaic; or one shot repeated into a field of 2 to 16 copies (in step or out of phase, optionally mirrored) or folded into a 2/4/6/8-segment kaleidoscope; optionally in a letterbox band (a 16:9 band across a 9:16 frame), stepping through layouts (3 → 4 → 6), drifting (a slow push, pull or pan over the field), ending with the last tile growing to fill the frame or the camera pushing into one tile. Reads file_ids (the clips, cycled over the tiles; one clip for repeat and kaleidoscope), points (kaleidoscope: its mirror centre on the shot), and the grid options layout (grid \| strips_v \| strips_h \| film_strip \| mosaic \| repeat \| kaleidoscope), tiles or steps, band, gutter, radius, reveal (pop \| slide \| wipe \| fade \| cut), merge, zoom_into, phase, mirror, drift. card_cascade: Two to nine rounded video cards (shadow, white edge, a slight tilt) drop onto a field one per half beat in a staggered grid, then the camera pushes in slowly; the field is paper, a blurred copy of the first clip, or the video below. Reads file_ids (the cards, in landing order), labels (a chip on each card), variant (paper \| blur \| none: the field), sound (each card heard until the next one lands). compare: Two to four clips frame-locked (one in-point) for an A/B: side by side or stacked with a thin divider, split on a slanted rule (diagonal), or as staggered framed boxes over a blurred copy (offset); panels slide in one per half beat, labels pop in, and replay ends on the last clip grown back to the full frame. Reads file_ids (the clips, in order: raw then edit), labels (one per clip: before, after), variant (side_by_side \| stacked \| diagonal \| offset; default by the frame's shape), replay (end on the last clip full frame), sound (keep the first clip's sound), backdrop (offset: false for the palette's field instead of the blur). window_cascade: Two to six clips in skewed parallelogram windows (clean slanted edges, pictures not sheared) arriving a few frames apart on one beat from alternate sides, then one pane slides to the centre and fills the frame (full bleed) on a later beat. Reads file_ids (the panes, left to right or top to bottom), highlight (0-based pane that goes full bleed; default the middle one). pass_wipe: A layer-pass breakdown: two to six frame-locked clips (plate, matte, CG, comp) stacked full frame, each wiped on over the last by a hard edge with a travelling hairline, one wipe per section, a stage label per pass. Reads file_ids (the passes, in order, frame-locked), labels (the stage names), variant (the edge travels right \| left \| down \| up). reflow: Two to nine footage cells re-lay themselves on the beat (grid → bento → one block, or the states you give): each cell is a window on its clip that moves and resizes with a steep ease-out, gutters steady, the footage keeping its scale. Reads file_ids (the cells, the first on top), states (layouts after the first: a list of box lists, one box per cell, centre x, y and size w, h 0-1). |
| `position_seconds` | number |  | Timeline start, seconds (default 0). Entrances land on the beats after it. (min 0) |

| `palette` | "ui_light" \| "ui_dark" \| "editorial" \| "callout" \| "tutorial" |  | Colours: ui_light, ui_dark, editorial (paper, ink, red, one blue), callout (dark, hot accent), tutorial (grid paper, ink, highlighter). Default per template. |
| `accent` | string |  | Replace the palette's accent colour (a brand colour): #rrggbb, #rgb, rgb(r,g,b) or a colour name. |
| `bpm` | number |  | Tempo of the beat grid, beats from the timeline's start or from offset_seconds (when there is no `beats`). (min 40, max 480) |
| `offset_seconds` | number |  | With bpm: timeline seconds of the first beat (default 0). (min 0, max 3600) |

| `button` | string |  | A button's label: type_search's search button, ui_cards' button the pointer clicks. |
| `tag` | string |  | A small tag: kinetic_type's (e.g. NO. 01), end_card plain's, step_card's label box, type_search's brand row, crop_labels' label prefix, callout's heading prefix (default ANATOMY). |
| `step` | integer |  | step_card: the step number. (min 1, max 99) |
| `highlight` | integer |  | kinetic_type: index of the word the highlighter marks; window_cascade: the pane (0-based) that goes full bleed. (min 0, max 30) |
| `sound` | boolean |  | card_cascade: each card plays its own sound until the next one lands; compare: keep the first clip's sound. Default: muted under the music. |
| `replay` | boolean |  | compare: end on the last clip alone, the split growing back into one full frame on a beat about 60 % of the way in. |
| `states` | object[][] |  | reflow: the layouts the cells move to after the first (a grid), one every two beats: each a list of boxes, one per file_id in order (centre x, y and size w, h, 0-1 of the frame). Default: a bento, then the first cell alone. |
| `variant` | string |  | grid_background: paper \| editorial \| dots \| plain; end_card: logo \| save \| plain; card_cascade: paper \| blur \| none (the field under the cards); compare: side_by_side \| stacked \| diagonal \| offset; pass_wipe: right \| left \| down \| up (the way the wipe's edge travels). |
| `align` | "left" \| "center" |  | Text alignment (kinetic_type, end_card plain). |
| `position` | "top" \| "center" \| "bottom" |  | Where the text sits (kinetic_type). |
| `backdrop` | boolean |  | Draw the template's own background (end_card and grid default true; type_search and word_scroll default false). |
| `font_family` | string |  | Set the template's type in a bundled family, drawn as outlines (same on every surface): inter (grotesk), anton (condensed), bebas-neue (condensed), archivo-black (display), instrument-serif (serif), space-mono (mono), varela-round (rounded), caveat-brush (hand), silkscreen (pixel). A mono family replaces the monospace labels. Default: the system sans. |
| `layout` | "grid" \| "strips_v" \| "strips_h" \| "film_strip" \| "mosaic" \| "repeat" \| "kaleidoscope" |  | grid: grid (2, 3, 4, 6 or 9 tiles), strips_v (vertical strips), strips_h, film_strip (small frames on sprocketed strips, the big frame last), mosaic (irregular, 3-9 tiles), repeat (one clip copied over 2/3/4/6/8/9/12/16 tiles: a multiplicity field), kaleidoscope (one clip in 2/4/6/8 segments, alternate ones mirrored so edges meet round the shot's centre). Default grid. |
| `tiles` | integer |  | grid: how many tiles (grid 2/3/4/6/9, strips 2-6, film_strip 3-7, mosaic 3-9, repeat 2/3/4/6/8/9/12/16, kaleidoscope 2/4/6/8). Default per layout (repeat 9, kaleidoscope 4). Tiles fill one per beat; a kaleidoscope's all at once. (min 2, max 16) |
| `steps` | integer[] |  | grid: tile counts for layout steps, increasing, e.g. [3, 4, 6]: the grid is re-cut on a beat for each and fills again. |
| `band` | string \| number |  | grid: confine the tiles to a band across the middle of the frame, as a ratio '16:9', '21:9' or a number (width / height); the rest is bars (backdrop). Default: the whole frame. |
| `gutter` | number |  | grid: gap between tiles, px at 1080 (default 6; repeat and kaleidoscope 0). (min 0, max 40) |
| `radius` | number |  | grid: tile corner radius, px at 1080 (default 0). (min 0, max 120) |
| `reveal` | "pop" \| "slide" \| "wipe" \| "fade" \| "cut" |  | grid: how a tile arrives on its beat: pop (springs up, default), slide (from the nearest edge), wipe, fade, cut (just appears; default for repeat and kaleidoscope). |
| `merge` | boolean |  | grid: end with the last tile growing to fill the frame. |
| `zoom_into` | integer |  | grid: end with the camera pushing into this tile (1-based, in the final layout) until it fills the frame; not with merge. (min 1, max 16) |
| `phase` | number |  | grid repeat: seconds each copy runs ahead of the one before, so copies move out of phase (default 0: in step; narrowed when the clip is too short). (min 0, max 2) |
| `mirror` | boolean |  | grid repeat: mirror alternate copies so their edges meet as mirrors (a kaleidoscope always is). |
| `drift` | "in" \| "out" \| "left" \| "right" \| "up" \| "down" |  | grid: a slow camera move over the whole field for the template's length: in (push in 12 %), out (pull out), left, right, up, down (pan). Not with merge, zoom_into, band or film_strip. |
| `transitions` | "auto" \| "none" \| "whip" \| "flash" |  | grid with steps: a motion transition on each re-cut, every kept tile moving together, in the same undo step: auto (default) = whip, one direction on every re-cut; flash: inverted frame, then glitch; none: plain cuts. |
| `strict_variety` | boolean |  | grid: refuse (nothing changes) when there are fewer file_ids than tiles on screen at once, so a clip would show in two tiles; the error says how many more. Default false: a warning. |

### kinetic_captions_tool

**Add kinetic captions** (direct tool). Animated word-by-word captions from the speech in footage clips (or from script cues when there is no transcribed voice), timed to each word, styled after creator and editorial reels: emphasis words picked automatically (numbers, stressed words) or given, laid out in the safe area for 9:16 or 16:9, in each shot's calm negative space and off the speaker's head (the boxes you give, else the subject matte's); with a subject matte the emphasis words go behind the head (creator, stack).

Surfaces: mcp, cli, editor. edits. Needs: media.

Availability: editor yes; cli yes; cloud yes (only when ffprobe is available); desktop — (web-only direct tool).

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `timeline_clip_ids` | string[] |  | Footage clips whose speech to caption (default: every clip with picture and sound; with cues, every footage clip under them). |
| `cues` | object[] |  | Script-timed words instead of speech (no voice, or a voice not transcribed): timeline seconds; a cue of several words shares its time between them by length. |
| `start_seconds` | number |  | Only words from this timeline time on. (min 0) |
| `end_seconds` | number |  | Only words before this timeline time. (min 0) |
| `style` | "creator" \| "documentary" \| "split" \| "karaoke" \| "stack" \| "editorial" |  | Look and motion (default creator). creator: word by word; emphasis huge red condensed capitals, connectors small white (creator talking heads). documentary: a phrase at a time, small white Inter on the lower safe line, soft fades (video essays, documentaries). split: two small words, one each side of the subject (storytelling, cinematic B-roll). karaoke: a line of bold capitals; the word being said lights up in an accent pill. stack: one condensed capital word per line, left aligned in the negative space, sliding up word by word. editorial: serif phrases centred, the emphasis word in italic accent, each word rising softly. |
| `emphasis` | string \| string[] |  | Words to emphasise: auto (default: numbers, stressed and long content words, never stopwords), none, or a list of words (an array, or one string separated by commas). |
| `avoid` | object[] |  | Boxes to keep captions off, 0-1 of the frame (centre x, y and size w, h): the speaker's face first (split puts its words either side of it). |
| `accent` | string |  | Emphasis / marker colour (#rrggbb or a name). Default per style (creator red, karaoke yellow). |
| `ink` | string |  | Colour of the other words (default white). |
| `text_size` | number |  | Connector word size, share of the frame's short side (style default: creator 0.046, karaoke 0.059, stack 0.11); emphasis words keep their ratio to it. (min 0.015, max 0.2) |
| `y` | number |  | Vertical centre of the captions, 0 top - 1 bottom (default: the style's own spots). Kept inside the caption safe area (on 9:16 out of the top 12 % and the bottom 20 %) and off the avoid boxes; split ignores it. (min 0, max 1) |
| `animation` | "pop" \| "slam" \| "slide_up" \| "rise" \| "fade" \| "tilt" \| "typewriter" \| "scramble" \| "letters" |  | How words enter, instead of the style's own. pop: scales up from half size with an overshoot. slam: lands from 1.8x size in 4 frames, cuts away. slide_up: slides up 3 % of the frame. rise: rises softly as it fades in. fade: fades in place. tilt: swings in rotated and overshoots; emphasis words stay turned 7 degrees. typewriter: typed letter by letter, no fade. scramble: emphasis words decode from random letters; the rest pop. letters: emphasis words bounce in letter by letter; the rest pop. |
| `behind_subject` | "auto" \| "emphasis" \| "all" \| "none" |  | Words behind the speaker (a cut-out of them above the captions): emphasis the emphasis words (set across the top of the head), all every word, auto (default for creator and stack) emphasis when the footage has a subject matte (generate_subject_matte_tool), else none. emphasis and all need the matte. |
| `placement` | "auto" \| "style" |  | auto (default): look at the shots - keep off the head (from the subject matte when no avoid box is given; where the host can matte, the CLI, it makes the matte of footage up to 40 s first, about a minute) and take the calmest, darkest of the style's spots; style: the style's spots in order. |
| `language` | string |  | Speech language when the clip has to be transcribed (auto by default). |

### place_on_word_tool

**Place on a spoken word** (direct tool). Land a title, sound effect, cutaway clip, motion block or cut exactly on a word of the speech (a pop-in on a keyword, a whoosh on 'boom', a cutaway when the product is named, a cut after a phrase): finds the word (or phrase, and which time it is said) in the timeline's transcripts, transcribing footage that has none, and runs the placing tool with its time set to the word's frame.

Surfaces: mcp, cli, editor. edits.

Availability: editor yes; cli yes; cloud yes; desktop — (web-only direct tool).

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `word` | string | yes | The spoken word, or a phrase of up to 6 words said one after another (case and punctuation ignored). |
| `occurrence` | integer |  | Which time it is said, 1 = first (default 1). (min 1, max 9007199254740991) |
| `every` | boolean |  | Every time it is said (at most 24) instead of one occurrence. |
| `anchor` | "start" \| "end" |  | Land on the word's first frame (start, default) or right after the phrase's last word (end). |
| `offset_frames` | integer |  | Frames before (negative) or after the anchor, e.g. -2 so a hit leads the word slightly (default 0). (min -60, max 60) |
| `what` | "title" \| "sfx" \| "clip" \| "motion_block" \| "cut" | yes | What lands on the word: title (add_kinetic_title_tool; text defaults to the word), sfx (add_sfx_tool), clip (add_clip_to_timeline_tool: a cutaway, needs file_id), motion_block (add_motion_block_tool, needs block), cut (split_clip_tool: splits the speaking clip there). |
| `args` | object |  | Arguments of that tool, without its time (position_seconds / at_seconds is set to the word), e.g. {recipe:'impact_punch'} for sfx, {file_id, duration_seconds:1.2, track:'V2'} for clip, {style:'creator', duration_seconds:1.5} for title. |
| `timeline_clip_ids` | string[] |  | Clips whose speech to search (default: footage with sound, and clips with a transcript such as TTS voices or aligned lyrics). |
| `language` | string |  | Speech language when a clip has to be transcribed (auto by default). |

**Insert B-roll on words** (direct tool). Cut away from a speaker to B-roll on the words a viewer wants to see (names, places, things, numbers; or the keywords you give), one cutaway every 5-8 s, 0.8-1.5 s each, never the same source twice: footage from the media bin (a file whose name or tags mention the word goes there), or stock found for each word (stock=true).

Surfaces: mcp, cli, editor. edits, open world.

Availability: editor yes; cli yes; cloud yes; desktop — (web-only direct tool).

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |

| `keywords` | string[] |  | Words or short phrases to cut away on, each at its first time said (default: picked from the speech: names, places, things, numbers). |
