### add_type_block_tool

**Add a type block** (direct tool). Typographic moves as native, editable title clips (outlined glyphs moved by keyframes; same on every Zenvi surface): text_on_path (a spinning ring of type, an arc, a wave), write_on (outlines or SVG paths drawn on stroke by stroke, then filled), stencil (the title as a window into the shot below, flying through a letter), echo_stack (copies that build out from the centre and collapse), strobe (a word every few frames on flipping full-bleed cards, ending on a lockup), wheel (a drum of words that snaps from one to the next), paper (paper-cut type boiling like stop motion, marks orbiting it).

Surfaces: mcp, cli, editor. edits. Needs: media.

Availability: editor yes; cli yes; cloud yes (only when ffprobe is available); desktop — (web-only direct tool).

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `block` | "text_on_path" \| "write_on" \| "stencil" \| "echo_stack" \| "strobe" \| "wheel" \| "paper" | yes | Which move. text_on_path: one line set along a ring (spins), an arc or a wave; caps with separators (·) read best on a ring; write_on: the text's outlines (or your SVG paths: a signature, an underline, an arrow, an icon) draw on along their paths, then the fill comes up; stencil: the text cut out of a full-frame card so the shot below plays inside the letters, a soft shadow in the cuts; it pushes in, then flies through a letter (open zoom) or cuts to the shot (open cut); echo_stack: copies of one line up and down the frame, the echoes outlined, arriving gap_frames apart from the centre out, then collapsing into the centre line; strobe: a word per hit on full-bleed cards hard-cut every hold_frames (or on beats), ground and ink flipping, the layout changing each cut (fit, bleed, outline, mirror, tall, stack), ending on a held lockup; wheel: words on a turning drum (a word flipper): it snaps from one word to the next every hold_frames (or on beats), the lines squashed, dimmed and blurred as they turn away; it rests on the last word; paper: type cut from paper (ink is the paper, accent the cut edge; the marks take accent, else the paper's colour) with a drop shadow, boiling like stop motion on twos, hand-drawn marks orbiting it. |
| `text` | string |  | The type: the ring's line, the words to write, the stencil title (1-2 words), the echoed line, or the strobe's words (split at spaces when there is no `words`). |
| `position_seconds` | number |  | Timeline start, seconds (default 0). (min 0) |
| `duration_seconds` | number |  | Length, seconds (default: text_on_path 3, write_on 2.5, stencil 2.4, echo_stack 1.8, paper 2.4, strobe the words' holds + 1.2 s of lockup, wheel its turns + 1 s). (min 0.2, max 30) |
| `font_family` | string |  | A bundled family, drawn as outlines (same on every surface): inter (grotesk), anton (condensed), bebas-neue (condensed), archivo-black (display), instrument-serif (serif), space-mono (mono), varela-round (rounded), caveat-brush (hand), silkscreen (pixel). Default: write_on instrument-serif; text_on_path, wheel and paper archivo-black; the others anton. |
| `font_weight` | integer |  | Weight for families that have several (inter): 100-900. (min 100, max 900) |
| `ink` | string |  | Colour of the type, all but stencil (default white; paper: the paper, default cream). |
| `ground` | string |  | stencil: the card's colour (default near-black); strobe: the first ground (default near-black; it flips with ink and accent). |
| `accent` | string |  | strobe: the third ground (default #ff3b1f); paper: the cut edge and the marks (default near-black). |
| `text_size` | number |  | Em size as a share of the frame's short side, all but strobe and write_on paths (default: fitted to the block). (min 0.02, max 1) |
| `x` | number |  | text_on_path, write_on, wheel, paper: horizontal centre, 0 left - 1 right (default 0.5). (min 0, max 1) |
| `y` | number |  | text_on_path, write_on, stencil, wheel, paper: vertical centre, 0 top - 1 bottom (default 0.5). (min 0, max 1) |
| `shape` | "ring" \| "arc" \| "wave" |  | text_on_path: ring (default; the line closes on itself), arc (over the centre), wave (across the frame). |
| `radius` | number |  | text_on_path ring/arc: radius as a share of the short side (default 0.3). (min 0.05, max 0.6) |
| `spin` | number |  | text_on_path ring/arc: degrees per second, clockwise (default: ring 40, arc 0). (min -720, max 720) |
| `paths` | string[] |  | write_on: SVG path data (the `d` of each path), drawn one after another in order; instead of text. |
| `view_box` | array |  | write_on paths: their viewBox [min x, min y, width, height] (default: their bounds). |
| `width` | number |  | write_on paths: width on the frame, share of the frame's width (default 0.6). (min 0.05, max 1) |
| `stroke_width` | number |  | write_on: stroke width, px at 1080 (default 3 % of the letter size; paths 1 % of the short side). (min 0.5, max 80) |
| `fill` | boolean |  | write_on: fill the shapes once drawn (default: text yes, paths no). |
| `draw_seconds` | number |  | write_on: seconds the strokes take (default 60 % of the block with a fill, 80 % without). (min 0.1, max 20) |
| `open` | "zoom" \| "cut" \| "hold" |  | stencil: zoom (default: flies through the fattest letter into the shot in the last 0.5 s), cut (the card cuts away on the last frame), hold (stays). |
| `shadow` | boolean |  | stencil: the soft shadow inside the cuts (default true). |
| `copies` | integer |  | echo_stack: copies including the centre line, odd (default 7). (min 3, max 13) |
| `echo` | "outline" \| "solid" |  | echo_stack: outline (default: echoes as outlines) or solid (dimmer fills). |
| `gap_frames` | integer |  | echo_stack: frames between one pair of copies and the next (default 2). (min 1, max 12) |
| `words` | string[] |  | strobe: the words, one per cut; wheel: the drum's lines in order, 2-12 (default: text split at spaces). |
| `lockup` | string |  | strobe: the held end card (default: the text, none when `words` come without it; empty string: none, the last word holds 0.4 s). |
| `hold_frames` | integer |  | strobe: frames each word holds (default 4, ~0.13 s at 30 fps: a strobe; 8-12 for a staccato list); wheel: frames each word rests before the drum turns (default 0.7 s); paper: frames per stop-motion pose (default 2). (min 1, max 90) |
| `beats` | number[] |  | strobe: timeline seconds to cut on instead of hold_frames (detect_beats_tool's beats moved to the music's position); a word per beat from the first one at or after position_seconds, the lockup on the next. wheel: the drum turns on these beats (the first n-1 after position_seconds). |
| `seed` | integer |  | paper: seed of the boil (default 1): the same seed boils the same. (min 0, max 2147483648) |
| `marks` | boolean |  | paper: the hand-drawn marks orbiting the word (default true). |
| `layouts` | "fit" \| "bleed" \| "outline" \| "mirror" \| "tall" \| "stack"[] |  | strobe: layouts cycled cut by cut (default all: fit, bleed, outline, mirror, tall, stack). |

| `recipe` | "whoosh_short" \| "whoosh_medium" \| "whoosh_long" \| "whoosh_rise" \| "whoosh_fall" \| "swish_airy" \| "whip" \| "impact_punch" \| "impact_thud" \| "impact_boom" \| "impact_slam" \| "sub_drop" \| "riser_noise" \| "riser_tonal" \| "reverse_swell" \| "ui_tap" \| "mouse_click" \| "keyboard_key" \| "toggle" \| "pop" \| "notification_blip" \| "typing_burst" \| "camera_shutter" \| "glitch_burst" \| "static" \| "sparkle" \| "hit_transient" \| "tail_bloom" \| "room_tone" \| "paper" \| "cloth" \| "swoosh_hit" |  | A procedural sound (list_sfx_tool describes each). | `provider` | "procedural" \| "openverse" \| "freesound" \| "kit" |  | With sound_id: the library of a search_sfx_tool result (openverse, freesound; procedural takes a recipe id), or kit for one of Zenvi's recorded sounds by its search_sound_library_tool id. |
| `sound_id` | string |  | With provider: the result's id. The sound is downloaded into the project, trimmed of silence, levelled like the procedural effects, and its licence and attribution are recorded on the file (list_credits_tool). |
| `title` | string |  | Freesound only: the result's title (a Freesound sound is found again by it). |
| `role` | "whoosh" \| "swish" \| "whip" \| "hit" \| "boom" \| "sub" \| "riser" \| "click" \| "pop" \| "glitch" |  | Library sounds: what it plays; its hit point and level follow (whoosh, swish, whip peak on the moment; hit, boom, sub, click, pop, glitch start on it; riser ends on it). Default: from its title and tags. |
| `max_seconds` | number |  | Library sounds: the longest it may run, seconds (default: the role's longest, e.g. 3 s for a whoosh). (max 15) |
| `allow_noncommercial` | boolean |  | Library sounds: accept a non-commercial licence (default false: refused). |
| `kit` | "recorded" \| "synth" |  | With a recipe: recorded (default where this surface can fetch it, unless pitch, brightness, intensity or pan shape a synthesised one) plays a real CC0 recording of that sound from Zenvi's kit, a different one than the kit sounds next to it; synth synthesises the recipe. Recipes the kit has no recording of (swoosh_hit) are synthesised. To pick a recording yourself: search_sound_library_tool, then provider=kit. |
| `at_seconds` | number |  | Timeline time of the moment, seconds. (min 0) |
| `clip_id` | string |  | Or: a timeline clip whose edge is the moment. |
| `edge` | "start" \| "end" |  | With clip_id: the clip's start (default) or end. |
| `marker_id` | string |  | Or: a marker's id; the moment is the marker's position. |
| `align` | "peak" \| "start" |  | peak (default): the sound's hit point lands on the moment (a whoosh's peak, an impact's transient, a riser's end). start: the sound starts there. |
| `gain_db` | number |  | Clip gain, dB, -40..0. Default: the recipe's mix level (peaks around -8…-14 dBFS, under music). (min -40, max 0) |
| `duration` | number |  | Seconds (each recipe has its own range; list_sfx_tool shows it). Default: the recipe's. (max 8) |
| `pitch` | number |  | Semitones, -12..12 (default 0). Lower = bigger and heavier. (min -12, max 12) |
| `brightness` | number |  | 0 (dark, distant) .. 1 (bright, close). Default 0.5. (min 0, max 1) |
| `intensity` | number |  | 0 (gentle) .. 1 (hard: more drive, tail and density). Default 0.7. (min 0, max 1) |
| `pan` | number |  | -1..1. Static sounds: the position. Moving sounds (whooshes, risers): the travel, from -pan to +pan (sign = direction). Default 0. (min -1, max 1) |
| `seed` | integer |  | Any integer: another variation of the same recipe (default 1). Vary it between repeats. (min -9007199254740991, max 9007199254740991) |

### spot_sound_tool

**Spot the edit for sound** (direct tool). The cue sheet of the edit, read-only: every hit point the eye registers (cuts, transitions, title and emphasis-word entrances, flash runs, keyframed moves and landings, speed-ramp hits, motion block events (clicks, toggles, typing, card lands, counter ticks, logo reveals) and 3D scene events (lands, bursts, spins), the music's climax), each with its time, kind, weight 0-1, role (hero, slam, transition, impact, ui, move, micro), screen x for pan, whether someone speaks over it, and whether the doctrine gives it a sound.

Surfaces: mcp, cli, editor. read-only.

Availability: editor partial (without audio decoding cuts are weighed by `beats` (when given) instead of the music and the climax comes only from `climax_seconds`; without the motion host, blocks placed before blocks recorded their events are spotted by their edges only); cli yes; cloud yes; desktop — (web-only direct tool).

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `genre` | "auto" \| "hype" \| "flash_montage" \| "saas_ui" \| "talking_head" \| "match_cut" \| "product_3d" \| "video_essay" \| "documentary" \| "editorial" \| "multiplicity" |  | The genre's palette: which cues, how dense, which space, its signature moves (CRAFT.md §10). auto (default) reads it from the edit: speech with captions = talking_head, speech = video_essay or documentary, UI blocks = saas_ui, 3D scenes = product_3d, tiles = multiplicity, 3-6 frame shots = flash_montage, fast cuts on music = hype, else editorial. |
| `beats` | number[] |  | Beat times on the timeline, seconds (e.g. build_reel_tool's `beats`), instead of analysing the music here. Every 4th is a downbeat. |
| `climax_seconds` | number |  | Where the climax is (a riser builds into it, an impact lands on it). Default: the music's biggest jump in loudness; none without music. (min 0) |
| `include_dry` | boolean |  | Also list the hit points the doctrine leaves dry (connector words, cuts inside a flash run, moves too small to whoosh), with why. Default false: counted only. |
| `limit` | integer |  | Most points listed (default 120); the counts cover all. (min 1, max 400) |

### auto_sound_design_tool

**Automatic sound design** (direct tool). Sound-design the whole edit in one step from its cue sheet (spot_sound_tool) in the genre's palette: layered hits (transient + body + sub with a phone harmonic + a tail in one shared space) on heroes, whooshes peaking on cuts and moves (pre-rolled, panned with the motion), clicks, toggles, typing and counter ticks on motion block events, micro sounds on glints and lands, a riser into the climax that stops a beat early with the bed sucked out under it, an ambience bed where the genre wants one, density held to the genre's band (cuts under speech and inside flash runs left dry), no recipe twice in a row, levels by role (hero, sweetener, micro).

Surfaces: mcp, cli, editor. edits, destructive. Needs: media.

Availability: editor partial (without audio decoding cuts are weighed by `beats` (when given) instead of the music, the climax comes only from `climax_seconds`, effects keep their designed levels instead of being levelled over what plays under them, and sources=library / mixed are refused; without Openverse library sounds come from Freesound (signed in); without the recorded kit's cache the sounds are synthesised (kit=synth)); cli yes; cloud partial (without audio decoding cuts are weighed by `beats` (when given) instead of the music, the climax comes only from `climax_seconds`, effects keep their designed levels instead of being levelled over what plays under them, and sources=library / mixed are refused; without Openverse library sounds come from Freesound (signed in); without the recorded kit's cache the sounds are synthesised (kit=synth); only when ffprobe is available); desktop — (web-only direct tool).

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sources` | "procedural" \| "kit" \| "library" \| "mixed" |  | Where the sounds come from: kit (default when the project has a sound kit: every cue plays through it), procedural (default otherwise: Zenvi's own sounds, see kit), library (licensed library sounds for every role, CC0 or commercial-use licences, credits recorded) or mixed (library whooshes, hits and risers; synthesised clicks, pops and subs). library and mixed use the kit's library sounds when it has them, else pick them now. |
| `kit` | "recorded" \| "synth" |  | Zenvi's own sounds: recorded (default where this surface can fetch it: real CC0 recordings, whooshes, punches, clicks, shutters, typing, never the same sample twice in a row; fetched once and cached) or synth (synthesised here, works offline). Plays every cue not taken from a library (about 500 recordings: sub drops, sparkles, risers and notifications too). Not with a project sound kit (sources=kit). |
| `intensity` | "subtle" \| "normal" \| "hype" |  | How much sound: subtle (only the big moments), normal (default: strong cuts, transitions, titles), hype (nearly every cut, tonal risers, sub drops). |
| `density` | "auto" \| "every_cut" |  | auto (default): the intensity's own spacing. every_cut: a sound on every cut, as hype edits have it (build_reel_tool's hype receipt asks for it): light hits and short whooshes alternating on the cuts, whooshes on whips, clicks on flashes and title slams, no sound twice in a row. |
| `genre` | "auto" \| "hype" \| "flash_montage" \| "saas_ui" \| "talking_head" \| "match_cut" \| "product_3d" \| "video_essay" \| "documentary" \| "editorial" \| "multiplicity" |  | The genre's palette: which cues, how dense, which space, its signature moves (CRAFT.md §10). auto (default) reads it from the edit: speech with captions = talking_head, speech = video_essay or documentary, UI blocks = saas_ui, 3D scenes = product_3d, tiles = multiplicity, 3-6 frame shots = flash_montage, fast cuts on music = hype, else editorial. |
| `seed` | integer |  | Another variation of the whole design (default 1). (min -9007199254740991, max 9007199254740991) |
| `beats` | number[] |  | Beat times on the timeline, seconds (e.g. build_reel_tool's `beats`), instead of analysing the music here. Every 4th is a downbeat. |
| `climax_seconds` | number |  | Where the climax is (a riser builds into it, an impact lands on it). Default: the music's biggest jump in loudness; none without music. (min 0) |

The motion transition presets (whip pans, zoom punches, zoom-through, spins, squash, shake, glitch, white/black/invert flashes, blur dissolve) with their directions and default lengths at this project's frame rate, the style mixes for apply_motion_transitions_tool, and the motion transitions already on the timeline.

Availability: editor yes; cli yes; cloud yes; desktop — (web-only direct tool).

No arguments.

### apply_motion_transition_tool

**Apply a motion transition** (direct tool). Put a motion transition on one cut between two clips that play back to back on a track (or, given both clip ids, on two tracks: one starts the frame after the other ends): whip pan, slide, zoom punch in/out, zoom through a point, spin, squash and stretch, shake, glitch, white/black/invert flash or blur dissolve.

Surfaces: mcp, cli, editor. edits.

Availability: editor yes; cli yes; cloud yes; desktop — (web-only direct tool).

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `preset` | "whip" \| "slide" \| "zoom_in" \| "zoom_out" \| "zoom_through" \| "spin" \| "squash" \| "shake" \| "glitch" \| "flash_white" \| "flash_black" \| "flash_invert" \| "blur_dissolve" | yes | Which transition: whip (left/right/up/down), slide (left/right/up/down), zoom_in, zoom_out, zoom_through, spin (cw/ccw), squash (left/right/up/down), shake, glitch, flash_white, flash_black, flash_invert, blur_dissolve. |
| `clip1_id` | string |  | Outgoing clip (the cut is at its end). With clip2_id omitted, the clip right after it on its track. |
| `clip2_id` | string |  | Incoming clip, starting the frame after clip1_id ends (on any track). |
| `track` | string |  | Instead of clip ids: the track of the cut (UI track number, 1 = bottom; name; or layer number) ... |
| `time` | number |  | ... and the cut's timeline time in seconds (the nearest cut within 0.5 s). (min 0) |
| `duration` | number |  | Length of the move in seconds, both clips together (default per preset, from docs/TASTE.md: whip 8 frames at 30 fps, zoom 7, spin 12, glitch 5, flash 3). (min 0.03, max 4) |
| `direction` | "left" \| "right" \| "up" \| "down" \| "cw" \| "ccw" \| "auto" |  | whip/slide/squash: left, right, up, down; spin: cw, ccw. auto (default) keeps the track's current: the direction of the previous motion transition on the track, else left (spin: cw). Keep one direction per sequence; up is a reserved accent. |
| `intensity` | number |  | 0.25-2, default 1: scales travel, zoom, blur and flash strength. (min 0.25, max 2) |
| `focus_x` | number |  | zoom_through: point to fly into, 0 = left edge, 1 = right (default 0.5). (min 0, max 1) |
| `focus_y` | number |  | zoom_through: 0 = top, 1 = bottom (default 0.5). (min 0, max 1) |

### add_plate_wipe_tool

**Plate wipe** (direct tool). Hide a cut behind an occluder plate: a blob, a burst, a disc or a sprite from the bin (splat, petals, a flag) grows from a point until it covers the whole frame exactly on the cut, holds a frame or two, then passes through the lens, shrinks back or flies off while the incoming clip pulls back behind it.

Surfaces: mcp, cli, editor. edits. Needs: media.

Availability: editor yes; cli yes; cloud yes (only when ffprobe is available); desktop — (web-only direct tool).

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clip1_id` | string |  | Outgoing clip (the cut is at its end). With clip2_id omitted, the clip right after it on its track (or the next scene). |
| `clip2_id` | string |  | Incoming clip, starting the frame after clip1_id ends. |
| `track` | string |  | Instead of clip ids: the track of the cut (UI track number, 1 = bottom; name; or layer number) ... |
| `time` | number |  | ... and the cut's timeline time in seconds (the nearest cut within 0.5 s). (min 0) |
| `plate_file_id` | string |  | A media-bin picture or video to use as the plate (a splat, petals, a flag; PNG with alpha, or a clip to screen). Default: a drawn shape. |
| `shape` | "blob" \| "burst" \| "circle" |  | Drawn plate: blob (default, an organic splat), burst (a spiky star) or circle. |
| `color` | string |  | Drawn plate's colour: #rrggbb, #rgb, rgb(r,g,b) or a name (default #ff5a36). |
| `x` | number |  | Where the plate grows from, 0 = left edge, 1 = right (default 0.5). (min 0, max 1) |
| `y` | number |  | 0 = top, 1 = bottom (default 0.5). (min 0, max 1) |
| `cover_seconds` | number |  | Time from a speck to covering the frame, ending on the cut (default 0.2 s: 6 frames at 30 fps; a fluttering flag 1.5 s). (min 0.03, max 2) |
| `hold_seconds` | number |  | Time the frame stays covered after the cut (default 2 frames). (min 0, max 1) |
| `exit_seconds` | number |  | Time the plate takes to leave (default 0.3 s). (min 0.03, max 2) |
| `exit` | "through" \| "shrink" \| "fly" |  | How it leaves: through (default: keeps growing past the lens and fades), shrink (back to its point), fly (off a side, see direction). |
| `direction` | "left" \| "right" \| "up" \| "down" |  | exit=fly: the side it flies off (default down). |
| `blend` | "normal" \| "screen" |  | normal (default) or screen (a bright sprite on black: only its light covers). |
| `cover_scale` | number |  | plate_file_id: the scale at which the sprite covers the frame (default 3). Drawn plates work it out. (min 1, max 30) |
| `pull_back` | boolean |  | The incoming clip arrives zoomed in and settles behind the plate (the zoom_out motion transition on the cut; default true). |

**Make a transition mask** (direct tool). Generate a luma wipe mask and add it to the media bin: square tiles that flip in a chosen order (a block/mosaic dissolve), concentric rings, or staggered bars, at the project's size.

Surfaces: mcp, cli, editor. edits. Needs: media.

| `order` | "random" \| "diagonal" \| "rows" \| "columns" \| "centre" \| "spiral" |  | tiles: the order they flip in: random (default), diagonal (a corner sweep, slightly ragged), rows, columns, centre (outward), spiral (from the edge in). |
| `count` | integer |  | tiles: tiles across the frame's short side (default 6: big blocks; 12 a fine mosaic); rings: how many (default 6); bars: how many (default 8). (min 2, max 24) |

### speed_ramp_tool

**Speed ramp** (direct tool). Change a clip's speed smoothly over time: the velocity edit (rush, near-freeze on the beat, rush again), a ramp-in or ramp-out, or a hero slow-mo.

Surfaces: mcp, cli, editor. edits, destructive.

Availability: editor yes; cli yes; cloud yes; desktop — (web-only direct tool).

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clip_id` | string | yes | Timeline clip id (from describe_project_tool, list_clips_tool or a receipt). |
| `preset` | "ramp_in" \| "ramp_out" \| "hero" \| "velocity" \| "custom" | yes | ramp_in: starts in slow motion and accelerates into normal speed. ramp_out: normal speed, then slows down to the last frame. hero: normal speed, a held slow-mo moment, normal speed. velocity: rush, near-freeze on the beat, rush again. custom: your own `points`. |
| `points` | object[] |  | custom: the speed (1 = normal) at each moment, seconds from the clip's start on the timeline clock, strictly increasing. The clip ends at the last point. |
| `ease` | "smooth" \| "out" \| "entrance" \| "in" \| "exit" \| "in-out" \| "in_out" \| "snap" \| "linear" |  | How the speed changes between points (docs/TASTE.md names). Default smooth. |
| `hit_at` | number |  | Timeline second (e.g. a beat from detect_beats_tool) where the slowest moment lands; hero, velocity and custom only. Default: the middle of the footage. (min 0) |
| `audio` | "mute" \| "keep" |  | mute (default) silences the clip: sound at 0.1x is pitched-down mush. keep leaves its volume alone. |
| `ripple` | boolean |  | Move later clips on the track by the change in this clip's length (default false: refuse when a longer clip would overlap the next one). |
| `allow_overlap` | boolean |  | Let a longer clip cover the next one. |
| `slow` | number |  | Speed at the slowest moment. Defaults: ramp 0.25, hero 0.25, velocity 0.1. (min 0.02, max 16) |
| `fast` | number |  | Speed outside the slow moment (the rush). Defaults: ramp 1, hero 1, velocity 2.5. (min 0.02, max 16) |
| `ramp_seconds` | number |  | Seconds each speed change takes (timeline clock). Defaults: ramp 1, hero 0.5, velocity 0.6. (min 0, max 30) |
| `hold_seconds` | number |  | Seconds held at the slowest speed. Defaults: hero 1, velocity 0.15. (min 0, max 30) |

### detect_onsets_tool

**Detect audio onsets** (direct tool). The transients of a clip's or a file's sound (hits, strikes, footsteps, door slams, consonants, drum hits) with how hard each one hits (0..1), and cut points proposed on the strongest ones at least min_shot_seconds apart.

Availability: editor yes; cli yes; cloud yes; desktop — (web-only direct tool).

| `file_id` | string |  | Media-bin file whose sound to read; times are seconds into the file. |
| `min_strength` | number |  | Weakest transient kept, 0..1 relative to the hardest hit (default 0.3). (min 0, max 1) |
| `min_shot_seconds` | number |  | Proposed cut points are at least this far apart (default 0.5): the strongest hits win. (min 0.05, max 30) |

### snap_cuts_to_onsets_tool

**Snap cuts to audio onsets** (direct tool). Move cuts onto the nearest strong audio transient within tolerance_frames (T040, cuts on in-world sounds): by default the incoming shot's own hit, so the shot opens on its knife strike, tool hit or footstep; onsets_from=outgoing ends the shot on its hit; onsets_from=clip with onset_clip_id snaps every cut to an SFX, ambience or music clip.

Surfaces: mcp, cli, editor. edits, destructive.

Availability: editor yes; cli yes; cloud yes; desktop — (web-only direct tool).

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clip_ids` | string[] |  | Clips whose incoming cut (their start) to snap. Default: every cut of `track`, or of every picture track. |
| `track` | string |  | Only cuts on this track (UI track number, name, or layer number). |
| `start` | number |  | Only cuts at or after this timeline second. (min 0) |
| `end` | number |  | Only cuts at or before this timeline second. (min 0) |
| `onsets_from` | "incoming" \| "outgoing" \| "clip" |  | Whose sound the transients come from: incoming (default; the next shot starts on its own hit, e.g. the knife strike), outgoing (the shot ends on its hit), or clip (onset_clip_id: an SFX, ambience or music clip). |
| `onset_clip_id` | string |  | onsets_from=clip: the timeline clip whose sound sets the hits. |
| `tolerance_frames` | integer |  | Farthest a cut moves, frames (default 4). (min 1, max 30) |
| `min_strength` | number |  | Weakest transient a cut snaps to, 0..1 (default 0.3). (min 0, max 1) |
| `lead_frames` | integer |  | Cut this many frames before the hit (default 0: the first frame of the shot carries the transient). (min 0, max 5) |
| `dry_run` | boolean |  | true: only propose the moves (nothing changes). |

### shot_length_ramp_tool

**Shot-length ramp** (direct tool). Cut an accelerating montage (T036): shots shorten along a curve from first_shot_seconds (default 2.5) to last_shot_seconds (default 0.4) over `shots` or duration_seconds, then optionally settle on a held shot.

Surfaces: mcp, cli, editor. edits.

Availability: editor yes; cli yes; cloud yes; desktop — (web-only direct tool).

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `file_ids` | string[] | yes | Media-bin videos and images that fill the shots, in order (round and round; each video continues where it was last cut). |
| `first_shot_seconds` | number |  | Length of the first shot (default 2.5). (min 0.1, max 20) |
| `last_shot_seconds` | number |  | Length of the last shot of the ramp (default 0.4). Longer than first_shot_seconds makes a decelerating ramp. (min 0.05, max 20) |
| `shots` | integer |  | How many shots the ramp has (default 12 unless duration_seconds is given). (min 2, max 300) |
| `duration_seconds` | number |  | How long the ramp lasts instead of a shot count: the count that fits the curve best, scaled to fill it. (min 0.5, max 600) |
| `curve` | "exponential" \| "linear" \| "ease_in" \| "ease_out" |  | exponential (default: each shot the same fraction shorter, the trailer feel), linear, ease_in (stays long, then collapses at the end), ease_out (drops fast, then steadies). |
| `settle_seconds` | number |  | A final held shot after the ramp, seconds (default none): the payoff the acceleration lands on. (min 0, max 20) |
| `settle_file_id` | string |  | What the settle shot shows (default: the next source in turn). |
| `motif_file_id` | string |  | A shot that comes back every motif_every shots, always from its first frame (a face, a logo, a recurring image). |
| `motif_every` | integer |  | Every how many shots the motif returns (default 4 when motif_file_id is given). (min 2, max 50) |

they rise in one by one and drift while the camera glides. icon_cube: A cube of glossy tiles (icons or colours on its faces) spins, then bursts into its cubelets. cube_cut: A transition: clip A on a 3D cube turns to clip B; first and last frames match the clips, so it sits seamlessly on the cut. glass_hero: An abstract hero object (morphing blob, torus, linked rings, sphere cluster) in glass, chrome or pearl, turning in coloured gradient light. particle_burst: Confetti, glowing sparks or glass shards bursting from a point, falling and tumbling. logo_extrude: The user's SVG logo (or a word) extruded and bevelled in chrome, glass, matte, clay or its own colours; | `role` | "whoosh" \| "swish" \| "whip" \| "hit" \| "boom" \| "sub" \| "riser" \| "click" \| "pop" \| "glitch" |  | What it plays; its hit point and level follow (whoosh, swish, whip peak on the moment; hit, boom, sub, click, pop, glitch start on it; riser ends on it). Default: from the prompt. |
| `at_seconds` | number |  | Timeline seconds to place it (its hit point lands there). Without it the sound only goes into the media bin. (min 0) |
| `align` | "peak" \| "start" |  | peak (default): the hit point lands on at_seconds. start: the sound starts there. |
| `gain_db` | number |  | Clip gain, dB (default: the role's mix level). (min -60, max 12) |
| `prompt_influence` | number |  | 0..1: how literally the prompt is followed (default 0.7; 0.6-0.8 repeats best). (min 0, max 1) |
| `loop` | boolean |  | Make a seamless loop (ambience beds). Default false. |

## Not ported yet

Zenvi desktop lists 169 tools. 5 are not ported yet (`packages/engine/src/tools/pending.ts`): no web surface lists them, and a call answers `Error: <tool> is not available in this Zenvi surface`. Their desktop schemas are in `schemas.gen.ts`. By desktop area:

- **MCP extras (desktop app plumbing)** (5): `capture_editor_screenshot_tool`, `get_log_paths_tool`, `send_assistant_prompt_tool`, `wait_for_editor_job_tool`, `zenvi_api_request`

Arguments of ported tools that only Zenvi desktop takes so far. A call that sets one to anything but its default is refused before anything changes (`Error: <tool> cannot use <argument> in this Zenvi surface yet …`, so the Assistant retries without it):

- `add_effect_tool`: processing

## Divergences from the desktop

Deliberate differences from the zenvi-core handlers:

- **tools that take timeline_clip_id**: A call that sends `clip_id` instead is accepted (the desktop refuses it) when the tool has no `clip_id` and the call does not also send `timeline_clip_id`; the receipt's warnings say to use `timeline_clip_id`. The same for `clip_ids` and `timeline_clip_ids`.
- **mcp_health_tool**: There is no Qt main thread to ask, so `main_thread_timeout_seconds` is accepted and unused; the call answering is the health check. The receipt adds whether Zenvi Motion blocks can render here (`data.motion.runtime`, with a warning when headless Chrome is missing; `setup_motion_runtime_tool` installs it).
- **detect_beats_tool**: Beats are a tempo-consistent grid, not the desktop's energy peaks. The tempo is moved into 80-180 BPM when the faster/slower pulse is in the audio, and the receipt adds `tempo` (confidence 0-1, the half/double readings in `alternatives`, beats_per_bar, bar_confidence) so a half- or double-time grid can be corrected with `bpm`. build_reel_tool and add_motion_template_tool also take `beats`, or `bpm` + `offset_seconds`, instead of detecting.
- **add_clip_to_timeline_tool**: Appending (no position_seconds) butts the clip against the last clip on the track. The desktop places it at `last_end + _one_frame` (tool_handlers.py:2726), leaving a one-frame black/silent gap.
- **add_clip_to_timeline_tool and the tools that place through it**: A host that cannot watch frames (no frame rendering or no Zenvi backend) counts as "not watched": a duration-only trim of a full video is refused instead of placing the first N seconds, and the result never says "(watched)". The desktop's watch falls back softly and places the window.
- **watch (add_clip_to_timeline_tool, slice_clip_at_best_match_tool, search_clip_scenes_tool, watch_clip_window_tool)**: Up to 12 frames rendered by the host; no ffmpeg scene-cut detection (shot cuts are always reported as none) and no near-duplicate frame dedupe (watch_window.py extract_watch_window).
- **apply_transition_tool**: clip2 defaults to the next clip on clip1's track instead of `Error: clip2_id is required` (tool_handlers.py:6645); no transition_name means fade (the desktop took the first file in its transitions folder).
- **reindex_project_file_tool**: "Already indexed" reads the current `ai_metadata.index` block (legacy `twelvelabs` as fallback); the desktop reads only `twelvelabs` (tool_handlers.py:7344). Re-uploading for indexing is not available on the web.
- **add_marker_tool / list_markers_tool**: A marker's name is stored as `label`; zenvi-core develop stores `name` (track_ops.add_marker). list_markers_tool, the marker tools and the web editor's ruler read either.
- **add_title_tool**: Templates are the 50 bundled ones (the desktop also lists the user's template folder). `template` can also be an existing .svg title: an absolute path read through the host's storage, or the path of a title in the project (Zenvi Cloud keeps titles at `@assets/title/…`). The title file is a new Project Files entry stored by the host (the CLI writes it to the project's assets folder, Zenvi Cloud stores it as project media).
- **add_animated_title_tool / list_title_templates_tool kind=animated**: The Blender templates are drawn as 2D titles: an SVG title animated with clip keyframes (scale, position, rotation, opacity) and the engine's Glow, Blur and LensFlare effects, so they render the same in the browser, the CLI and the cloud and stay editable. Extrusion, bevel, lighting, particles and 3D camera moves are approximated or dropped. Template names, parameters, defaults, validation and the length (template frames × length_multiplier, remapped for the project frame rate like Blender) are the desktop's; earth, magic_wand, snow and picture_frames_4 are 3D scenes and are refused as desktop-only; spacemovie_intro and colors place three clips in a row; timeout_seconds is accepted and unused. kind=animated lists `renders_here` and `look` per template and a `renderer` block where the desktop reports its Blender setup.
- **edit_title_tool**: The edited title is a new Project Files entry that takes the old one's place in every clip and in the bin (scope=all_clips), in the same undo step; the desktop points the same entry at the new SVG and keeps its file_id. Web hosts store media by content and never change the bytes behind a file id. The receipt's file_id is the new entry's.
- **titles, captions and timers: fonts**: add_title_tool and edit_title_tool check a font against the fonts the host renders titles with, where it can list them (FrameHost.fontFamilies: render-node's font index on the CLI, which is the computer's fonts plus the bundled Lato, and in Zenvi Cloud, whose image has DejaVu, Liberation Sans / Serif / Mono and Lato; on both, Arial, Helvetica, Times and Courier count as installed where a Liberation or Croscore twin draws them with the same widths, as fontconfig substitutes them on Linux), with the desktop's matching, close-match suggestions and Title Editor fallback for a template font that is not installed. The web editor's browser does not list its fonts, so there a font is taken as given (one it lacks falls back to another), as the desktop does when Qt cannot tell. Captions and timers take fonts as given everywhere; the desktop drops a caption preset's font (thinning its outline) when that font is missing.
- **add_effect_tool**: Stabilizer, Tracker, Object Detector and Object Mask, whose OpenCV analysis the desktop runs when they are added, are refused as not available here, like process_clip_effect_tool, and `processing` (their analysis options) is not ported. Outline (also OpenCV) is added for Zenvi desktop to draw, with a warning that the web editor, the CLI and Zenvi Cloud render the clip without it.
- **set_project_setting_tool**: A size or frame rate no built-in profile has needs a custom profile, which only Zenvi desktop's profiles folder keeps (the CLI writes it there, like set_project_profile_tool); the web editor and Zenvi Cloud refuse it. save_as_default keeps the sample rate and channels as defaults for new projects in an editor's own settings when they have such entries; the web editor's have none (its new projects start at 48000 Hz stereo) and the CLI and Zenvi Cloud have no editor settings, so it is refused there before anything changes, with the reason. saved_as_default says whether defaults were kept (the desktop echoes the argument).
- **list_title_templates_tool**: kind=static lists the 50 bundled templates; the web has no user template folder. kind=project reads each title through the host's storage (bundled emoji through the assets).
- **add_emoji_tool / search_emojis_tool**: The desktop's 1,239 OpenMoji SVGs ship with the engine (assets/emojis, minified without changing what they draw; scripts/gen-emojis.mjs) and are stored as `@emojis/<file>` like the desktop stores them. There is no user emoji folder (group 'user' finds nothing). duration_seconds 0 is 10 s, the desktop's Default Image Length preference default.
- **list_captions_tool / edit_captions_tool / remove_captions_tool**: They work on Caption effects, as on desktop develop (made by add_captions_tool, Zenvi desktop or the Caption effect). With no target the project's only caption track is used: the web has no effect selection to pick from.
- **speech: get_transcript_tool, transcribe_media_tool, remove_words_tool, export_captions_tool, add_captions_tool, duck_under_speech_tool**: Speech recognition runs on the Zenvi server (`POST /api/v1/transcription`, zenvi-backend #67: OpenAI whisper-1, 2 credits per started minute, a Zenvi sign-in), not on device. The host sends mono 16 kHz speech audio (MP3 from ffmpeg on the CLI and in Zenvi Cloud, WAV from Web Audio in the editor), long media in pieces split at pauses. A file's words come from, in order: a transcription kept on the file, the media index's transcript cues (word timings estimated by character count: `transcriptionSource: "index_cues"`, `wordTiming: "estimated"`), then a new transcription (`transcriptionSource: "server"`, `wordTiming: "exact"`). The words are kept in the project on the file (`ai_metadata.asr`: the desktop transcript cache record's fields plus the segments and the media's content hash), outside the undo history, so the next call, another surface or an exported .zvn reuses them and undoing an edit keeps them; the desktop caches on disk and ignores the key. Whisper leaves out "um" and "uh" unless prompted, so English and auto-detected requests carry OpenAI's filler prompt; words take the punctuation of the server's segments, like faster-whisper's. Without a target only clips with a picture and sound are transcribed (audio-only clips such as music beds only when the timeline has no such footage, or when named). modelId and engine are accepted and unused (one server model). A server without the route answers in words: `speech recognition is not available yet on this Zenvi server`.
- **add_captions_tool**: Transcript captions: the desktop reads only the index's transcript cues (shared out by character count); here a clip's words come as for get_transcript_tool, and recognized words keep their own timings: captions break at sentence ends, at pauses over 0.8 s and where the desktop's line-breaking costs put them (maxWords, maxChars), each runs from its first word to its last and stays up across a short pause. Subtitle files are read through the host: from disk on the CLI, from the project's files in Zenvi Cloud and the editor.
- **remove_words_tool**: Cuts on real word timings only (a kept or new transcription, never the index's estimates). wordIndices must come from the words they cut: indices for a transcription made by the same call are refused (call get_transcript_tool first), and a transcription made after the index's words gets the next transcriptGeneration, so indices read from the index are refused as stale. Refusals that need no words (an unknown fillerPreset, a retimed clip, an ambiguous clipId) come before any transcription is paid for.
- **duck_under_speech_tool / analyze_timeline_audio_tool**: With speech_clip_ids=auto and no indexed speech, talking footage (picture and sound) without a transcript is transcribed and its words become the speech windows (`transcript`); the desktop falls back to its local VAD. A kept transcription also marks a clip the index does not know as speech in analyze_timeline_audio_tool.
- **remove_silence_tool**: Speech windows come from the desktop's energy VAD run on the host's RMS envelope (AudioHost.analyzeAudio), not from on-device VAD models.
- **web-only arguments**: Hosts without a playhead or local file paths, and the CLI, need a few arguments the desktop's schemas do not have (scripts/tool-schema-overlay.json `web_extra_props`): add_marker_tool label/text and add_track_tool label (older names for `name`), save_project_tool path, set_clip_volume_tool volume/gain/db, set_clip_speed_tool clip_id/factor/direction (the web's older speed tool: one clip id, speed, backward = reverse), list_effects_tool category (older name for kind), remove_effect_tool effect_id (the older tool's one id, added to effect_ids), watch_clip_tool file_id/timeline_clip_id, import_stock_media_tool position_seconds/track/duration_seconds/start_seconds (place the import), detect_beats_tool bpm (track the beats at a given tempo). Every argument the desktop accepts is accepted; the ones only the desktop handles so far are refused (see Not ported yet).
- **desktop defaults the web does not follow yet**: save_project_tool and export_video_tool replace an existing file (the CLI's) where the desktop refuses unless overwrite=true; new_project_tool / open_project_tool have no unsaved-changes guard (every web surface autosaves, so discard_unsaved is accepted as is); generate_tts_and_add_to_timeline_tool defaults to the track below the picture, where the desktop picks or creates a free narration track.
- **tools zenvi-core develop rewrote as editor tools**: get_project_info_tool, list_markers_tool, new/open/save_project_tool, play_tool, add_track_tool, add_marker_tool, generate_tts_and_add_to_timeline_tool and set_keyframes_tool take develop's schemas; their results keep the earlier text and receipts (develop answers with structured receipts). set_keyframes_tool animates the seven earlier properties (develop: any keyframable clip property) with develop's point times, interpolation, ease presets and modes, and refuses a point without a value (develop keeps the curve's value there).
- **split_file_add_clip_tool**: require_visual_match reads true/false; the desktop's `bool(...)` treats the string "false" as true (tool_handlers.py:2370).
- **wait_for_editor_job_tool (desktop MCP extra, #237)**: Pending, and likely to stay so: tool calls here run to completion inside the call, so there is never a detached editor job; the name gets the standard not-available refusal.
- **argument coercion**: As zenvi-core normalize_args, plus numbers/booleans become strings for string-only properties (MCP clients send typed JSON). Tools that are editor tools on the desktop coerce like its @editor_tool registry (`_registry.coerce_args`): case-insensitive enums, "1.5s", comma-separated or JSON lists, "y"/"n"; an empty string or null for an argument that cannot hold it means its default where the desktop refuses it, and a value that cannot be coerced is refused in the web's words (`Invalid arguments for …`) rather than the registry's.
- **add_clips_to_timeline_tool**: image_seconds=0 and transition_seconds=0 mean the desktop's default Default Image Length (10 s) and Default Transition Length (1 s): the web has no preferences.
- **separate_clip_audio_tool**: With to_track the audio clip goes straight there. The desktop first splits it onto the track below (creating a track when the clip is on the bottom one) and then moves it, which can leave that new track empty.
- **set_clip_audio_video_tool**: The web timeline draws the waveform of every clip with sound and has no per-clip switch: waveform=show changes nothing and waveform=hide is refused (in words the Assistant retries without it). The desktop stores waveform samples in the clip (`ui.audio_data`).
- **reverse_clip_tool**: A clip on a locked track is refused; the desktop's handler reverses it anyway (its Time menu skips the lock check).
- **apply_clip_preset_tool**: Runs the engine's port of the clip menu's handlers (ops/presets.ts, also behind the web editor's clip menu) as of develop: fade lengths, the combined in-and-out fade, motion zone lengths and the wipe-out masks. crop / crop_resize add the Crop effect with a new effect id and do not select it (the desktop also selects it and shows its transform handles). An Emphasis preset without at_seconds starts at the host's playhead: the saved playhead on the CLI and in Zenvi Cloud.
- **seek_playhead_tool**: In the web editor it moves the editor's playhead and reports where it is. The web editor's playhead stops at the end of the last clip, so a time past it is reported there with a note (the desktop goes there and shows black). Without a preview (CLI, Zenvi Cloud) it moves the playhead saved with the project (`playhead_position`, where the web and desktop editors open), with no undo step, and play=true is refused; previous/next marker then has no selection to follow. Playback is checked before the playhead moves (the desktop moves, then refuses to play from the end).
- **get_playhead_and_selection_tool**: Without an editor (CLI, Zenvi Cloud) it reports the saved playhead, playback stopped, and `selection` and `view` as null (`saved: true`). In the web editor the zoom is the editor's pixels per second as `seconds_per_100px`, and `timing` is null: the web timeline has no timing mode.
- **set_timeline_view_tool / select_timeline_items_tool**: They need the web editor. Zoom steps are the editor's own (×1.5); a range or visible_seconds zooms and scrolls the editor's timeline within its zoom limits, and the receipt reads the view back. The web timeline has no timing (retime-by-drag) mode: timing=true is refused, timing=false is already so. The Properties panel shows one effect: selecting effects selects the last one named together with its clip, and the receipt says so.
- **update_marker_tool / remove_marker_tool**: A marker's name is read from `name` (desktop) or `label` (the web's add_marker_tool); a rename writes it where the marker keeps it, and a marker without a name gets `label`. The web editor's ruler shows either. Times past the end of the timeline are checked against the length the desktop keeps (at least 300 s and 10 s past the last item).
- **colour frames (analyze_frame_colors_tool, chroma_key_clip_tool, inspect_color_tool, match_color_to_reference_tool, the after previews of apply_color_tool / apply_look_tool)**: Frames come from the host's renderer (the one the person sees) and are measured with a port of libopenshot's FrameScope; the desktop renders on a private libopenshot timeline. A clip alone is rendered twice (as is, and with a Negate after its transform) to recover the transparency the host's opaque frames do not carry. analyze_frame_colors_tool measures frames at most 960 px wide (the desktop: the project size). The web editor stays editable while frames render (the desktop renders on its GUI thread), so chroma_key_clip_tool and match_color_to_reference_tool write nothing, and say so, when the clip was edited meanwhile.
- **analyze_frame_colors_tool**: save_frame_path is not written (web surfaces write no files): the analyzed frame is attached to the result (`frame_attached: true`, with a warning).
- **chroma_key_clip_tool**: Without frame rendering, key_color='auto' is refused, 'green' / 'blue' key the stock shade (the desktop's fallback when sampling fails) and keyed_pct is null.
- **LUTs (list_luts_tool, color_grade_clip_tool, update_effect_tool lut_path, apply_color_tool, apply_look_tool)**: The 50 built-in LUTs are bundled with every renderer and stored as `@colors/<category>/<name>.cube`, the alias the desktop writes on save, so they render the same everywhere. A .cube file outside them is accepted where the host reads local files (the CLI) once it parses the way libopenshot loads it, and refused elsewhere. list_luts_tool lists the built-ins (the desktop also lists the user's LUT folder).
- **apply_color_tool, apply_look_tool, inspect_color_tool, list_looks_tool, match_color_to_reference_tool**: The result is the desktop's JSON object, as the summary and as `data`. Preview frames are attached as images (MCP image content, the Assistant's image sidecar) and their `*_preview_jpeg` fields name the attachment (`attached image 1`) instead of carrying base64. Scopes give clipped shadows/highlights as shares of the frame (0-1), which the nuke-risk, outdoor and match-loop thresholds expect; the desktop passes FrameScope's pixel counts to them.
- **match_color_to_reference_tool**: The grading passes run on a working copy and the final grade is one undo step; a pass the desktop would abort halfway (a merged saturation below 0.5) refuses before anything changes. referenceImagePath needs local file access (the CLI).
- **process_clip_effect_tool**: Refused on every web surface: Stabilizer, Tracker, Object Detector and Object Mask run OpenCV analysis (libopenshot ClipProcessingJobs) inside Zenvi desktop. The effects it adds play back there; the web renderers pass them through, and list_effects_tool marks them `renders_on_web: false`.
- **list_project_files_tool / remove_files_from_project_tool scope='missing'**: `missing` is the host's check (MediaHost.missing): the CLI looks at the disk (an image sequence by its frames, like the desktop), the web editor at the media it could load (what Project Files offers to relink), Zenvi Cloud at the uploads; a host without the check reports null and refuses missing_only / scope='missing'. `optimized_preview` is always none, since only Zenvi desktop makes and plays optimized previews. `path` is the path as the project holds it (the desktop reports an absolute local path).
- **update_project_files_tool**: Relinking (path, search_folder) needs local file access, so the CLI only: the CLI imports the new media under its own rules (a file in the OS temp folder is copied into the project's assets folder, and gets the desktop's fingerprint, so same_content works) and searches at most 5,000 files of a folder (the desktop: 20,000). The web editor relinks with Relink… in Project Files; Zenvi Cloud refuses it.
- **import_image_sequence_tool**: Needs a host that reads local folders (the CLI), which probes the `%04d` pattern like FFmpegReader and renders one image per frame at the chosen rate (checked pixel for pixel against libopenshot's Timeline). A sequence is no single file to upload, so the web editor and Zenvi Cloud refuse the import and cannot play one a desktop project brings. skip_indexing is accepted and unused (the web does not index on import). When a folder holds more frames than the CLI lists (5,000), frames and last_frame come from the frames ffmpeg plays.
- **update_transition_tool / add_transitions_between_clips_tool masks**: A mask given as an image file path is read only where the host has local files (the CLI); elsewhere the path is matched as a name, so pass mask_file_id with a project image. Masks resolve by the desktop's names and aliases (transition_ops.find_transition) and also by catalog id and `@transitions/` path. duration_seconds=0 uses the engine's default transition length (1 s); the desktop reads its Default Transition Length preference, which ships at 10 s.
- **copy_transition_tool**: With fit_duration only the pasted curves are fitted to each target's length; the desktop also rescales the target's other curve in place (media_files_transitions.py:711-716), which moves the inner points of a curve that has more than two.
- **transition targets (update/reverse/remove/copy_transition_tool)**: An id given twice in transition_ids is acted on once (the desktop reverses it twice, back to where it was). scope='selected' reads the web editor's selection; without an editor it finds none.
- **generate_image_and_add_to_timeline_tool**: Where the image would go (position_seconds, the track, a locked track) is checked before the backend is asked, so a typo spends no credits; the desktop generates first and then reports a placement it cannot make. When the placement fails after generating (the track was locked meanwhile in the editor), the image stays in Project Files and the answer is an applied receipt with its file_id and the desktop's "Do NOT regenerate" line, which the desktop sends as an error. The host stores the image as generated_<12 random characters>.<ext>: in the project's assets folder on the CLI, as content-addressed `@assets/generated/` media in Zenvi Cloud, in browser storage in the editor.
- **ingest_web_video_tool (decision: web pages are fetched only on the person's own computer)**: The zenvi CLI and `zenvi mcp` fetch a web page's video with the yt-dlp program the person installed (the desktop ships yt-dlp as a Python module; `zenvi doctor` checks for it, ZENVI_YT_DLP sets its path); without it a page link is refused in words, and direct media links (.mp4, .mov, .webm, .mkv, .avi) still work. Zenvi Cloud and the web editor refuse in words: a hosted server or a browser fetching third-party pages is a different legal and terms-of-service position from a person's own computer, and it gets server addresses blocked. Their refusal points to a direct link to the media file (import_media_from_url in Zenvi Cloud, import_video_url_and_add_to_timeline_tool) or an upload. On the CLI the intents, the job budgets (about 25 s, then status=running with a job_id; a job_id call waits up to about 45 s; a second call for the same link joins the download) and the JSON answers are the desktop's, as `data`; the import and placement happen in the call that finds the download finished, as that call's one undo step (the desktop's download thread imports when it lands), and `zenvi call` follows a running job to the end. Failures are error receipts (`Error: <reason>`) carrying the desktop's ok=false object, which the desktop sends as an applied JSON answer. A placement that cannot work (a bad position, an unknown or locked track) is refused before anything is downloaded. A link that ends like a video file but answers with a web page (a Wikimedia Commons `File:….webm` page) is read as a page; the desktop downloads the page itself as the video and fails to import it. Videos are cached for seven days under the Zenvi cache folder, named after the page, and copied into the project's assets folder when imported (the desktop re-encodes them to generated_<id>.mp4).
- **list_comfyui_templates_tool, list_comfyui_jobs_tool, create_media_with_comfyui_tool, enhance_file_with_comfyui_tool, cancel_comfyui_job_tool, prepare_recording_tool**: Refused on every web surface. The ComfyUI tools drive the ComfyUI server on the person's own computer that Zenvi desktop connects to (Preferences > AI > ComfyUI URL, blank = off) through its template registry, generation queue and workflow graphs; no web surface has that integration, and Zenvi Cloud and the browser cannot reach a local server. prepare_recording_tool sets up the desktop's Recording dock (microphone, screen and webcam capture). The refusals name what works here: generate_image_and_add_to_timeline_tool, generate_video_and_add_to_timeline_tool and generate_tts_and_add_to_timeline_tool.
- **list_recent_projects_tool / open_project_tool recent_index**: Each surface lists what it has as recent projects: the CLI reads Zenvi desktop's File > Recent Projects on the same computer (its settings file; projects the CLI opens are not added, since only the desktop app writes that file); the web editor lists the projects stored in this browser and Zenvi Cloud the person's cloud projects, most recently edited first, at most 10, with the project id as `path`. `current_path` is the open project's file or id. recent_index opens one where open_project_tool works (the CLI).
- **forget_recent_projects_tool**: Refused on every web surface: the web editor's and Zenvi Cloud's lists are the projects themselves (forgetting one would delete it), and the CLI's is Zenvi desktop's, kept in a settings file only the desktop app writes (zenvi-core keeps even its own headless sessions from writing it).
- **list_recovery_versions_tool / restore_recovery_version_tool**: The CLI lists and restores the copies Zenvi desktop zips into its recovery folder each time it saves the project (matched by the project's exact name, newest first); the CLI's own saves make no copies, so a project only the CLI has saved has none. Restoring keeps the current file as `<name>-<time>-backup.zvn` and reopens the project, like the desktop; discard_unsaved is accepted and unused (every web surface saves each change). The web editor and Zenvi Cloud keep only the latest version of a project, with its undo history, and refuse.
- **export_project_file_tool / import_project_file_tool**: Refused on the web surfaces: EDL and Final Cut Pro XML are conversions of the Zenvi format, implemented once in Zenvi desktop (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §4, the handoff rule). zenvi and zenvi mcp run the call in the desktop app while it has the project open.
- **consolidate_project_media_tool**: The CLI only (local files next to a saved project): collect copies outside media into `<project>_assets/media` (one undo step points back at the originals) and reclaim deletes copies whose recorded original is byte-identical, saving the project before it deletes anything, like the desktop. Media in the web editor and in Zenvi Cloud is stored with the project already, so they refuse.
- **reset_caches_and_history_tool**: playback_cache clears the web editor's filmstrips and waveforms and redraws the preview; the CLI and Zenvi Cloud render every frame from the project, keep no cache and answer `unchanged`. waveforms drops the desktop's stored waveform samples (`ui.audio_data`) as one undo step; web timelines draw waveforms from the media and store none. undo_history forgets every step, and the next save writes no history.
- **get_editor_layout_tool / set_editor_layout_tool**: The web editor's panels: Project Files, Effects, Transitions, Titles, Stock and Generate share the left side (one shows at a time), Properties and Assistant the right; Video Preview and Timeline always stay. The `simple` view is the editor's starting arrangement, and the desktop's dock names and aliases work for the panels both editors have. It has no Color Grade or Recording view, scopes, saved custom views, floating panels (dock_all changes nothing) or toolbar to hide, and a browser enters fullscreen only from a click or a key press: those are refused before anything moves. The CLI and Zenvi Cloud have no editor window and refuse.
- **get_preferences_tool / set_preference_tool**: The web editor's own settings, in the desktop's entry shape: Snapping (Timeline) can change; Enable Autosave (always on), History Limit (50), Backend URL and the keyboard shortcuts (Zenvi desktop's defaults) are read-only and say why. Values are checked with the desktop's rules (types, ranges, choices, shortcut syntax and conflicts). Zenvi desktop's other preferences (cache, decoders, theme, autosave interval…) do not exist here and are refused as unknown. The CLI and Zenvi Cloud have no editor settings and refuse.
- **video profiles: list_project_profiles_tool, set_project_profile_tool, set_project_setting_tool, manage_custom_profiles_tool, new_project_tool profile**: Custom profiles live where Zenvi desktop reads them, its profiles folder (`~/.openshot_qt/profiles`): the CLI lists, creates, edits and deletes them there, so a profile made on either shows on the other, and a size or frame rate no built-in profile has gets a `Custom WxH fps` profile like the desktop's. The desktop re-applies a project's named profile when it opens it (HD 720p 30 fps when it does not know the name), so the web editor and Zenvi Cloud, which cannot reach that folder, list the built-in profiles only and refuse to make a custom one, and manage_custom_profiles_tool. set_default is refused everywhere: the default profile is a desktop preference in its settings file. delete checks the open project's profile, not the desktop's default one.
- **list_export_presets_tool**: `available` means the engine's exporters write the preset's container (mp4, mov, mkv, webm, gif, mp3, wav; not AVI, MPEG, OGG or DVD) and the host can encode its codecs (AAC always counts, as on the desktop): the CLI asks its ffmpeg, the web editor its browser, Zenvi Cloud the ffmpeg its renders use. The user's own presets folder is Zenvi desktop's, so only the built-in presets are listed.
- **export_video_tool, get_export_settings_tool, set_export_setting_tool**: One plan for every surface, ported from develop's build_export_plan (presets/plan.ts): the preset by title, everyday name (webm, prores, gif, mp3) or social name (tiktok, reels), the quality it offers, the profile it allows closest to the project (with develop's re-framing note), All Formats bitrates from the frame, the call's Advanced overrides, then the defaults set_export_setting_tool stored (checked and stored under develop's keys; keys an earlier web version stored as given, such as start in seconds or fps, are still read), the range (whole = first clip to last clip, selection, custom start/end) in frames of the export's rate, and the output path. Before anything renders the host says whether it writes the container and encodes the codecs; a codec the call or a stored setting named is refused with the ones the host has, a preset's audio codec the host lacks is replaced by one it has in the same container, with a warning (WEBM (vp9) gets Opus where ffmpeg has no libvorbis), as AAC always counts on the desktop. An export at another frame rate renders with every keyframe rescaled to it, as the desktop does. interlaced is refused everywhere: no web encoder interlaces. Per surface: the CLI renders with its ffmpeg and writes the file: relative paths, and the default folder, start at the project's folder (the desktop's default is its Export folder preference), `~` is the home folder, and it writes MP4, MOV, MKV, WebM, GIF, MP3, WAV, FLAC, M4A and PNG, JPG, BMP or TIFF image sequences (not AVI, MPEG, OGG, DVD or PPM). The web editor renders in the browser (MP4, MOV, MKV, WebM with the codecs the browser encodes, and WAV), which downloads the file under file_name (else the project's name): folder is refused and output_path only names the file; range='selection' uses the editor's selection. Zenvi Cloud starts a render job and answers with its render_id (get_render_status returns the download link), one file per render (no image sequences), folder refused. Differences from the desktop: an existing file is replaced (the desktop refuses unless overwrite=true); a size no profile has is rendered without saving a custom profile; a stored image_format applies (the desktop's default image_format='png' hides it); there is no one-export-at-a-time lock (each render writes under a staged name and moves into place).
- **save_frame_image_tool**: The frame is rendered at the project's size by the host's renderer. The CLI writes the file (a relative or empty file_path starts at the project's folder; the desktop's default is its export folder); the web editor downloads it (a download never replaces a file); Zenvi Cloud keeps it with the project's exports, answers with a download link (24 hours) and renders PNG only (a .jpg request is saved as .png, with a warning). A host that saves no files attaches the frame to the result instead. An existing file is found when writing, after the frame is rendered (the desktop checks first).
- **export_files_to_folder_tool**: Files keep the desktop's export names. The CLI copies into the folder (relative to the project's folder; empty = the project's folder) and renders sub-clips and image sequences to H.264/AAC MP4 at the file's size and rate (quality 22, written under a staged name, then moved into place); the web editor downloads each file, rendering sub-clips in the browser; Zenvi Cloud answers with a download link per file (24 hours) and refuses sub-clips and image sequences (render_project renders timelines). The receipt's `folder` says where they went.
- **summary previews**: `…` is written as U+2026; the desktop's file had the mojibake `ΓÇª` (ai_metadata_utils.build_summary_preview).
